015cbcbb-d80c-5c50-bcc8-c90cabc986b0.name: Cadillac Series 75
015cbcbb-d80c-5c50-bcc8-c90cabc986b0.description:
Known for its luxurious and powerful vehicles, Cadillac produced several cars equipped with large V8 engines between the 1930s and the 1980s. Of those models, the Series 75 is the best known. Differing in size and bodywork as well as the level of trim, the Series 75 models were most popular among Cadillac’s affluent clientele. In the post-war period, they were the most prestigious automobiles in the United States of America, and it is not surprising that in 1947, the firm produced 59,436 units.  
  
That same year, the Portuguese government sanctioned the purchase of two identical Cadillac Series 75s, one for the President of the Republic – Óscar Carmona – and the other for the President of the Council of Ministers – Prof. António de Oliveira Salazar. Before that, all official vehicles were standardised on make and models. All ministers had Packard Clipper cars, with eight cylinders and seven seats, while the secretaries and under secretaries of states drove cars were of the same brand, but with five seats.  
  
Salazar always used his allocated Cadillac until his death in 1970, even refusing a Mercedes-Benz 600 acquired by the Ministry of Finance in 1968—a car now under the Presidency of the Republic. He claimed that the Cadillac was still in good condition and served him very well in his official capacity.  
  
In April 1971, less than a year after Salazar’s death, the Cadillac Series 75 was sold at auction and was then acquired by João de Lacerda to be exhibited at the Museu do Caramulo. Interestingly, the interior of the model remains in perfect condition, having been protected with seat covers by order of Salazar himself.

021ca6c1-9f8d-5f9a-87db-f4c9193cbe1f.name: Saint John the Baptist from a Deesis Tier
021ca6c1-9f8d-5f9a-87db-f4c9193cbe1f.description: John the Baptist was the cousin of Jesus Christ and preached in the Judean desert. He lived a life of self-denial by wearing camel hair clothing and eating only locusts and wild honey. The people of the region came to him to be baptized in the Jordan River. When Jesus asked to be baptized, John proclaimed that he was not worthy of such a task and that Christ should baptize him instead. Christ insisted, however, and during the baptism the Holy Spirit descended and a voice from heaven proclaimed, “This is my beloved Son in whom I am well pleased” (Matthew 3:17). John got into trouble when he criticized King Herod’s marriage to Herodias, who had a child from her previous marriage to Herod’s brother. Herod’s stepdaughter, Salome, convinced him to arrest John and demanded his head on a silver platter. Granting her wish, Herod ordered John beheaded. In this icon, John the Baptist stands in three-quarter profile and faces left. This icon was once part of a Deesis tier of an iconostasis and would have hung to the right of an icon of Christ in Majesty.

keywords: Saints; Religious iconography

06ec7051-a897-50d7-b81b-d66f8f20eaf6.name: Studebaker Electric
06ec7051-a897-50d7-b81b-d66f8f20eaf6.description:
This burgundy vehicle represents one of the world’s first electric cars. 100 years before Tesla launched their first electric roadster in 2009, Baker Motor Vehicles had already manufactured this car.  
  
The “electric carriages” emerged as more tasteful, quiet and pollution-free alternatives to steam and gas-powered wagons. Less prone to catch fire or soil clothes with oil, the car would spark a special interest in high-society women. A closer glance reveals the expensive silk and fabric that cover every interior surface.  
  
A century ahead of the modern electric-car-era, charging stations would power the Studebaker Electric all across towns like New York, allowing the 12 six-volt batteries to run up to 5 hours with range of 170 km.

0bbaf404-0e91-5630-bcc7-37cb18ebe36e.name: Lion of St. Mark
0bbaf404-0e91-5630-bcc7-37cb18ebe36e.description: The silver lion of St. Mark was a gift from Venice to the council and citizens of the city of Zurich in 1608. At that time, Venice was being besieged by Austria and Spain and sought contact with Protestant cantons; the Venetian ambassador Padavino, who wrote extensively about his trip, was sent to Zurich. His account of the banquet to celebrate the presentation of the lion he had donated contains the report that the lion was circulated in a round of toasts: the head can be removed and used as a tumbler.

0cc82bad-3c43-57b4-a06b-eee73296523f.name: Jana o’ Narr Dress
0cc82bad-3c43-57b4-a06b-eee73296523f.description: Dress with wide sleeves and made of white cotton and silk with red, green, and thin, dark blue stripes. The chest panel has striped Kashmir fabric with wavy edges. The neck and shoulders have additional silk cloth and braid work surrounding the chest panel. The sleeves have silk fabric (“bird’s tongue”) in addition to the original cotton fabric colour. The front and back panels have no embroidery work, and the border is done in wavy needlework. This dress is handmade by the women of Tubas (in the Nablus district) for special occasions and weddings. Traditional Palestinian costumes reflect complex social systems that express the owners’ social status, wealth, region and origins through different designs and decorative elements. In this case, both married and single women can wear this dress, but it is usually worn by the wealthy class of women because the fabric is very expensive and not easy to obtain. Wearing this dress is a visual statement that the owner of the dress is from the upper class of society.

0decaa99-5256-5760-8c07-88af6780788c.name: Honda NR 750
0decaa99-5256-5760-8c07-88af6780788c.description: Showing off its technological advance, Honda launched the spectacular Honda NR in 1991. At the heart of the NR is a 750 cc, V4 engine with unique, oval (instead of round) pistons and a whopping eight valves per cylinder. It is essentially a V8 masquerading as a V4. Together with the single-sided swingarm, carbon fairing, titanium-treated cowling and under- saddle exhausts, the NR was not only technically unique, but also a forerunner in terms of design. Only 300 examples were built of Japanese designer Mitsuyoshi Kohama's piece de résistance, with a cost of 2.3 million Belgian francs at the time, or around €55,000.

0e5a35d3-747a-518d-a5ff-8fd46510b6e9.name: Alba
0e5a35d3-747a-518d-a5ff-8fd46510b6e9.description:
The Alba metallurgical plant in Albergaria-a-Velha was in the early 1950s a large industrial plant belonging to Comendador Martins Pereira. His son António Augusto Martins Pereira, a motorsport enthusiast, wanted a brand purely dedicated to racing. Hence the Alba car brand was born. The first Alba was designed and built in 1952, and as was normal at the time in Portugal, France and Italy, it was equipped with the highly reliable 1089cc Simca-Fiat engine. The Alba’s styling was quite remarkably ahead of its time, especially when put next to other cars of the time, such as the DM or the FAP. Both the DM and FAP had comparatively very archaic aesthetics.  
  
The Alba racing team achieved early success in the hands of Martins Pereira and Francisco Corte Real Pereira. The latter, who helped develop the car, won the 1100cc class Boavista Circuit race two years in a row in 1951 and 1952. With three racing cars built, the company focused its competitive efforts on national events. Corte Real was usually at the wheel for circuit events and Martins Pereira competed in regularity tests and rallies.  
  
In 1954, the ACP, Portugal’s motorsport governing body, imposed new regulatory changes which increased engine capacities from 1 litre to 1.5. Small Portuguese builders like Alba had to find new engines if they were to comply. Alba began to develop several engines initially by increasing the bore of its 1.1 litre unit to 1.3. The company also later did a similar job on a Peugeot block.  
  
But with the rapid ascendancy of the Porsche engine, which proved to be unbeatable in both the Denzel and 550 Spyder, Corte Real Pereira devised a daring plan to help Alba compete. Taking an old Alfa Romeo 6C 1.7-litre unit, the company then reduced the bore size to 1.5, thus developing a curious 1.5 litre six-cylinder engine. The newly equipped Alba raced in Boavista 1955 and 56, then in Vila Real 1958, without much success.  
  
Alba’s life in competition continued for some time without notable success until 1961, when Corte Real Pereira finished third in the Rally Nocturno de Salgueiros.

0fae2309-f11c-5cf4-a9a0-0bd126c69093.name: A picture from the very beginning
0fae2309-f11c-5cf4-a9a0-0bd126c69093.description: The oldest photograph in the collection of the National Museum is in essence a photo montage. The photographer touched up the boundaries of the individual component photographs and coloured the composite. Johann Baptist Isenring was one of the first Swiss photographers. He mounted the first photographic exhibition in St. Gall as early as 1840.

1027a1b3-31c5-5bc1-9a9d-4a4a487bcc6d.name: Char-de-côté diligence
1027a1b3-31c5-5bc1-9a9d-4a4a487bcc6d.description: The British publisher John Murray travelled through the canton of Jura by stagecoach in 1838. He later described the trip in his *Hand-Book for Travellers* as “very rough” – hardly surprising, since the travelogue author was riding in a char-de-côté. On this type of coach, which was used primarily in France and western Switzerland, the carriage body was set at right angles to the undercarriage, so that the passengers sat sideways (*de côté*) in relation to the direction of travel. This was more uncomfortable, but it allowed these carriages to be built with a narrower wheelbase, and as a result the char-de-côté could be used even on those roads in the canton of Jura that were narrower than the standard track width of 1.4 metres. Today, no travel writer would have cause to complain about the quality of Swiss public transport, which is one of the best in Europe.

1203d512-7e1e-58c1-b5ee-087144132528.name: The Miracle of Saint George and the Dragon
1203d512-7e1e-58c1-b5ee-087144132528.description: Saint George was born to Christian parents in the 3rd century. He joined the Roman army and became a high-ranking officer at a young age, earning the respect of Emperor Diocletian. At that time, Diocletian persecuted Christians and required that all soldiers offer sacrifices to the pagan gods. Saint George publicly denounced the emperor and confessed to being Christian. He was subjected to brutal punishments but refused to renounce his faith. Eventually, he was beheaded and became a popular martyr saint. In one story of his life, he rescued a town besieged by a dragon. The townspeople had been sacrificing children, who were randomly chosen by casting lots, to the dragon. Saint George rode in just as the town’s princess was to be sacrificed. He killed the dragon, a symbol of paganism, and converted the townspeople to Christianity. In this icon, Saint George rides a white horse and slays the dragon with a spear while Christ, seen in the upper right corner, bestows a blessing.

12f7ae35-34a3-5118-bed7-7ea23f024c4b.name: Volkswagen Kübelwagen
12f7ae35-34a3-5118-bed7-7ea23f024c4b.description:
The genesis of Volkswagen was with the KdF-Wagen (“Strength Through Joy vehicle”) launched in 1938 by the German government. After World War II, this model became known as the “Beetle”. In parallel, two military models were built with the capacity to face inaccessible terrain. Such was the versatility of not only this small car but also the Volkswagen engineers and the brand itself.  
  
With the outbreak of World War II, the popular KdF-Wagen was adapted by Ferdinand Porsche to meet the needs of the German army. Out of that came two all-terrain vehicles that stake their claim in history as Volkswagen’s first: the Kübelwagen and the Schwimmwagen.  
  
Using the KdF-Wagen’s four-cylinder engine along with the chassis and torsion bar suspension, the Kübelwagen was developed by Ferdinand Porsche for tactical support and military transport purposes. It was widely used in combat by German forces in North Africa and the campaign on the Russian front.  
  
Although it was known internally as Type 82, it quickly gained the nickname *kübel-wagen*, or the “Bucket Car,” because of its shape.  
  
Even without the four-wheel drive of its Jeep opponent, the Kübelwagen used the excellent traction of the KdF-Wagen chassis and drive to move over rough terrain, while the inverted wedge shape of its bodywork and tall ride height allowed it to pass unscathed over the most difficult routes.

13838f38-9d4c-5ce5-b63d-fabe43b3504a.name: «Holbein table»
13838f38-9d4c-5ce5-b63d-fabe43b3504a.description: The table known as the «Holbein table« is one of the most important and most mysterious items in the furniture collection. Until 1965 it was attributed to the Basle painter Hans Holbein the Younger. It was only investigations by the Swiss National Museum in Zurich that revealed the true name of the artist as Hans Herbst. Painted table tops were a popular form of art in the Renaissance. They told stories, but above all represented the expert art knowledge and importance of the person who commissioned them, who has immortalised himself with a coat of arms and that of his wife in the middle of the table. They were Hans Bär and Katharina Brunner. Bär was a textile merchant in Basle and enlisted with foreign armies in the important function of standard bearer. He was killed at the battle of Marignano in 1515. The black background of the table imitates a slate on which various objects have been drawn, which, at a closer glance, turns out to be six allegorical scenes. To achieve as true-tolife an impression as possible, the artist used the trompel’oeil technique, creating an optical illusion, and distributed random objects across the table top such as playing cards, a pair of spectacles and a seal stamp bearing his name.

14f845c7-6932-510e-b7b4-091796f3db1b.name: Lancia Delta Integrale HF
14f845c7-6932-510e-b7b4-091796f3db1b.description:
The journey from the every day car to track hero: this is the common story that has summed up the rise of the iconic cars of motorsport mythology. The Lancia Delta is no exception. Conceived in 1979 by Giorgio Guigiaro, the model was based on the Fiat Ritmo platform, sufficient for the ambitions of a small family car with some modestly luxurious add-ons.  
  
The first sports version was presented in 1986, and it used a two-litre four-cylinder engine with a turbo-compressor, an eight-valve head, and a four-wheel-drive system.  
  
The first of the 1987 versions of the Lancia Delta Integrale 8V, also called the Delta 4WD, was homologated by the Italian brand to be used on competition stages. The quietly understated family car would go on to dominate the World Rally Championship for several impressive years. Its four-cylinder block was fitted with a five-bearing crankshaft and an aluminum head with double camshafts controlling two valves per each 84mm × 90mm cylinder. An IAW-Weber multipoint electronic system and a Garret AiResearch turbocharger allowed the Lancia to output 185cv at 5300 revolutions per minute, whilst its maximum torque of 304Nm was achieved at 3500 revolutions per minute.  
  
To send power to the wheels, an integrated transmission was used as well as independent suspension on both axles with MacPherson struts, helical springs, telescopic dampers, and stabiliser bars. The rack and pinion type steering was hydraulically assisted, and disc brakes were fitted to all four wheels.  
  
The original road-going Delta Integrale was not impressive by any means, but it still allowed Lancia to have a solid base from which it could develop a rally car in the mid-1980s. The brand turned the docile family car into the fabulously performing Delta S4 Group B rally car before the class was banned for being too dangerous.  
  
In 1989, Lancia presented a 16-valve version of the Delta Integrale, increasing the engine output to 200cv.  
  
The company followed up in 1991 with another update, the first Evoluzione model, known in some markets as the Deltona. The Evoluzione was easily recognizable by its bodywork extensions and additional air intakes. Engine output was increased to 210cv at 5750 revolutions per minute through the use of a Garret T3 turbo-compressor and intercooler. The transmission on the Evoluzione was also upgraded with a planetary central differential, viscous multi-disc clutch and a Torsen rear differential, allowing a forward-rearward power distribution of 47–53 percent.  
  
Although the benchmark performance improved slightly, with the Lancia Delta Integrale HF Evoluzione, the main differences from its predecessors was its impeccable behaviour and driveability on the demanding rally stages – demonstrated by its success in multiple World Rally Champion.  
  
Two years after the emergence of the first Delta Evoluzione, Lancia presented the Delta Integrale HF Evoluzione II, aesthetically similar to its predecessor but with a reprogrammed Magneti-Marelli IAW electronic management system, which raised the engine to 215cv. Interestingly, this version was not used for FIA homologation purposes, as it was equipped with a smaller low-inertia turbo which made the engine docile at low speeds.  
  
Considered even today as the most successful model in the history of the World Rally Championship, the Lancia Delta Integrale clinched a remarkable total of six world titles.  
  
This car was donated to the Museu do Caramulo by Ilídio de Oliveira Freitas.

15c6cc0c-756e-54f3-b8c1-d90de5905a43.name: Ford Model T Truck
15c6cc0c-756e-54f3-b8c1-d90de5905a43.description:
This extraordinary truck popularised the American movie-snack-popcorn. The Columbia Buddy Company customised one of three Ford T-Model to become a popcorn-machine and vending machine on wheels.  
  
Aside from fresh-buttered popcorn fried with the original Cretors popcorn equipment, this crimson red carriage would sell ice-cold sodas and hot-roasted peanuts.  
  
Although special purpose vehicles were not an unknown concept, as T-Models were also transformed into ambulances and fire trucks, the popcorn wagon presented a unique marketing and entertainment opportunity with its charming circus aesthetic.

17dd3ddc-9ae3-581d-8b9f-700deb1e3f48.name: Omega Speedmaster Watch
17dd3ddc-9ae3-581d-8b9f-700deb1e3f48.description: When the American astronaut Buzz Aldrin walked on the surface of the moon on 21 July 1969, he was wearing an Omega Speedmaster wristwatch. Originally, Neil Armstrong was supposed to wear a similar watch when, prior to Aldrin, he became the first human being to set foot on the moon. However, after the moon lander’s clock broke during the approach, Armstrong decided to leave his Speedmaster in the lander just to be on the safe side. These watches, made in the Swiss city of Biel, had been chosen by the US space agency NASA because of their superior quality: Omega watches were simply better than any competing timepiece and the Speedmaster, made in the Swiss canton of Berne, was the only model that was found to be spaceworthy after stringent testing. The watches were tested under conditions of zero gravity, extreme temperatures, and high acceleration. Thus the Omega Speedmaster became the only representative of Switzerland ever to reach the moon.

187e2883-937a-528a-9be3-eb2a76a5653a.name: Peugeot Bebé
187e2883-937a-528a-9be3-eb2a76a5653a.description:
In 1896, Société Anonyme des Automobiles Peugeot appeared on the scene after Armand Peugeot parted ways with Company Les Fils de Peugeot Frère. From then on Peugeot dedicated itself to the construction of automobiles. Five years later, in 1901, the brand launched a small model at their Paris showroom. Named “Bébé” and designed for the general public, the car was equipped with a small 652cc single-cylinder engine. Production of the first “Bébé” however, would not last very long. Peugeot was unable to sell many of these small cars and so decided to discontinue the model. As the new century dawned, Peugeot began the development of a new prototype with the help of Ettore Bugatti. At around the same time, on the other side of the Atlantic, the lion mark achieved an impressive victory in the gruelling Indianapolis 500 motor race.  
  
The car that accomplished that incredible feat, with driver Jules Goux, was with the first model ever to be equipped with a four-cylinder engine and two overhead camshafts.  
  
The victory and collaboration with Bugatti gained huge popularity for the French mark, and they followed up at the Paris Motor Show with the launch of the Bugatti Type 19 which was set to be manufactured in Sochaux by Peugeot.  
  
The Type 19 was christened the “Bébé”, a nickname in jest, alluding to the car’s tiny size. This time around, the newly resurrected “Bébé” would be hailed as a true utility vehicle. The car was a marked improvement over the first “Bébé” both in terms of technology and performance.  
  
What distinguished this new “Bébé” from its rivals was the quality of Bugatti’s work and Peugeot’s rigorous manufacturing processes. The collaboration yielded a car that was extremely user friendly and economical. It was also very rapid considering its tiny size, topping off at a maximum speed of 60 km/h.  
  
The car’s 6hp advanced mono-block engine was equipped with T-valves which allowed it to rev to 800 revolutions per minute.

1a6fd108-7bb7-5e52-b70a-6d8c81c37f18.name: Battle-shield with coat of arms inspired by Oriental motifs
1a6fd108-7bb7-5e52-b70a-6d8c81c37f18.description: Some people like to claim that everything used to be better in the old days. Indeed, the oldest extant battle-shield, too, once shone in bright colours. Analysis has shown that, 800 years ago, the greyish green used to be a vibrant blue. The lion, too, wasn’t always as lacklustre as it is now; it used to stand out in shiny silver leaf. The shield belonged to the noble von Brienz family, which used to hold feudal rights in today’s Canton of Uri, on the road to the Gotthard pass. When its owner, the knight Arnold von Brienz, died in 1225, his battle-shield was placed above his tomb in commemoration of his deeds. This is how it survived the ages. The shield’s many notches, holes and nicks remind us of the brutal reality of medieval battles.

1cd784d6-18b3-56c5-be73-779aee36490e.name: Widow’s Dress from Bir al-Sabe
1cd784d6-18b3-56c5-be73-779aee36490e.description: A dress for widowed women only, from Bir al-Sabe. This dress displays heavy embroidery work on the chest panel, similar to a *qalayed* (necklace) motif. The embroidery of this dress is less festive and detailed and adorned with few birds or flower motifs. The neck and shoulders are embroidered on each side and display orange *hirmizi* needlework with few flower shapes. The sleeves show varied embroidery designs, while the *banayeq* (side panels) and the front and back panels show heavy embroidery work in blue with cypress tree and feather motifs, along with talismans on the top of the side panels. This dress has a very unusual and interesting feature; at the bottom of the dress (*dyara*) there is thick blue embroidery, but the dress is devoid of embroidery in the middle. This design feature holds deep social meaning, denoting that the owner of the dress is a widowed, unmarried woman who does not intend to marry again. On the other hand, if the woman fills the gap in the middle with embroidery, this added embellishment is a declaration of her intention to marry again.

1e900f37-1b9d-5993-8da8-4990a85354e3.name: Ford Model T Touring
1e900f37-1b9d-5993-8da8-4990a85354e3.description:
This weathered wagon personifies one of the most influential cars of the 20th century – the Ford T-Model. Production numbers peaked in the 1920s as demand rose from around the globe due to their affordable price and high-quality materials.  
  
The American owner of this Touring-model would spend most of his days keeping to himself out in the forest. In addition to the soft-top and storm curtains that provided ample protection in any weather and terrain, the farmer equipped the car with a net to entrap rabbits and snakes and drums for transporting milk.  
  
In 1924, more than half of all cars sold worldwide were T-models, making this car a recognisable collectible whilst also encapsulating the adventures of different people such as this huntsman.

20abb534-7f0e-5447-96ad-59b7c1f4354d.name: Pendant with The Miracle of Saint George and the Dragon
20abb534-7f0e-5447-96ad-59b7c1f4354d.description: Saint George was born to Christian parents in the 3rd century. He joined the Roman army and became a high-ranking officer at a young age, earning the respect of Emperor Diocletian. At that time, Diocletian persecuted Christians and required that all soldiers sacrifice to the pagan gods. Saint George publicly denounced the emperor and confessed to being Christian. He was subjected to brutal punishments, but refused to renounce his faith. Saint George was beheaded and became a popular martyr saint. In one story of his life, he rescued a town besieged by a dragon. The townspeople had been sacrificing children, who were randomly chosen by casting lots, to the dragon. Saint George rode in just as the town’s princess was to be sacrificed. He killed the dragon, a symbol of paganism, and converted the townspeople to Christianity. In this miniature icon, Saint George is seen atop a white horse slaying the dragon with a spear. The princess stands nearby with the town in the background. The icon has a beautiful enameled *oklad* (frame) with a silver loop at the top. It may have been worn around the neck and was probably commissioned for a military officer from a wealthy family since Saint George is a patron saint of soldiers.

materials: Egg tempera on wood with silver oklad, gems, enamel

211781ad-6226-573b-b2c2-fd83e8a3b8d0.name: Ornamental vase
211781ad-6226-573b-b2c2-fd83e8a3b8d0.description: Clement Heaton (1861–1940) created this spectacular vase in Neuchâtel around 1895. It fuses the traditional art of the coppersmith and the cloisonné enamel technique that he mastered to perfection. When he moved to Switzerland from England, Heaton brought with him the ideals of the Arts and Crafts Movement that sought to achieve a revival of handicrafts. Quality craftsmanship should enjoy the same status as traditional art forms and be recognizably different from mass-produced goods. Around the turn of the century, Heaton was among the most innovative craftsmen and decorators working in Switzerland. Besides cloisonné, he also specialized in embossed wallpaper and monumental stained glass windows. For the front elevation of National Museum Zurich, he produced mosaics to designs by Hans Sandreuther (1850–1901). After a fire destroyed his workshop, Heaton moved to the USA in 1914 and continued his career there.

2158b63f-20c0-52d3-a46b-eed9cff3a8ed.name: Tarf I

In 1957, with a four-cylinder Gilera 350 cc engine developing 40 HP at 11,500 rpm, seven new records were set. The 1957 model, on display here, is capable of traveling at up to 212km/h.

23a85edf-b1ca-5f3a-83c4-cac1414d6670.name: Alfa Romeo GP Tipo 158

2489eb40-b999-5440-ab39-000e178dc3e2.name: BMW Isetta 300
2489eb40-b999-5440-ab39-000e178dc3e2.description:
This BMW Isetta represents the only microcar from the 1950s from a manufacturer still existing nowadays. The cream car features one front-opening door that swings out with the instrument panel exposing the steering wheel.  
  
In post-war Europe, BMW struggled with declining sales of their expensive models. Upon acquiring manufacturing rights from the Italian refrigerator company Iso Rivolta, BMW built their motorbike one-cylinder engine into the tiny coupe.  
  
Soon, the car would become a best-seller until the bubble-era’s end in 1962. Using the autobahn, the Isetta found its way across the Alps back to Italy’s mountainous roads for summer holidays. Today, collectors everywhere celebrate the clever and minimalist vintage car.

25d3e4e9-78d3-5af6-a091-db51a68ac649.name: Panhard & Levassor 16/18HP
25d3e4e9-78d3-5af6-a091-db51a68ac649.description:
The first Panhard & Levassor car debuted at their Paris showroom in 1889. It was originally fitted with one of Gottlieb Daimler’s engines, who licensed it to René Panhard and Emile Levassor. The Panhard & Levassor 16/18HP in the Museu do Caramulo was purchased by João de Lacerda in December of 1955. It was purchased from the car’s first owner, Marquis de Santa Iria, D. José Luiz de Vasconcelos.  
  
As is fitting for a Panhard & Levassor, the car was finished at the request of the Marquis himself at the Carrosserie Jansen in Paris, where it was fitted with a six-seater “brougham” body and the passenger cabin lined in velvet. The elegant Panhard & Levassor then entered Portugal on 12 April 1927.  
  
Since its acquisition by the museum, the French car has had a minor mechanical restoration and an exterior paint touch-up. Currently, the odometer reads 55,000 km.

2715f2b5-ca2e-5d2e-b004-073279cd0cb4.name: Delage D8-120 D'Ieteren
2715f2b5-ca2e-5d2e-b004-073279cd0cb4.description: Although Lancia adopted unibody construction as early as 1922, the traditional ladder chassis – onto which independent coachbuilders would mount bespoke bodies – remained influential in the interwar period: brands like Bentley, Rolls-Royce, Bugatti, and other big names of the interwar period remained loyal to the latter. Even after the devastating stock market crash of 1929, renowned names such as Farina, Gangloff, Chaprón, Saoutchik, Gläser, Erdmann & Rossi, Castagna, Touring Superleggera, Mulliner, and James Young continued to craft extravagant designs with seductive shapes. In contrast to the prêt-à-porter approach of vehicles like the Citroën Traction Avant, this haute couture was almost always handcrafted, ensuring that no two models were ever identical. These celebrated vehicles frequently won prestigious awards at *concours d'elegance* events, where the elite would then take the winning car home. Like fashion houses, the coachbuilders would always attach their logos to the fronts and rears of the cars, while the actual designers remained anonymous. In Belgium, D'Ieteren and Vanden Plas– both coachbuilders dating back to the 19th century– stood out in particular. As breathtaking as this Delage with a D'Ieteren body may be, by 1939 it was already a giant out of touch with the changing zeitgeist. This rigidity spelled the end for companies like Delage, Delahaye, Bugatti, and most coachbuilders, especially as the economic situation forced European manufacturers to develop affordable cars for the common man.
2715f2b5-ca2e-5d2e-b004-073279cd0cb4.author: Ahmed Chaouch
keywords: Pre-war luxury; custom body; coachbuilt; aluminium

275cc0ff-de13-5c3a-adca-a82522ceaf51.name: Daimler 420 Saphire Majestic

Manufactured by the Daimler Company, this Saphire Majestic features a Jaguar six-cylinder engine, 165 horsepower and the luxury comparable to a Rolls Royce. Meant as a town car for the elite, the chauffeur's partition lends privacy to the passengers in the back.  
  
A wooden cabinet hides a state-of-the-art television for entertainment on longer drives, while the performance of the car allowed it to compete with sports cars of the day.

2c70068a-7308-58bd-8e5c-6c1e519d536e.name: Ferrari 166MM Barchetta Touring
2c70068a-7308-58bd-8e5c-6c1e519d536e.description:
The Ferrari 166 MM Barchetta Touring was first unveiled at the Turin Motor Show in September 1948, where the brand established itself as a motorsport icon – a status that endures to this day.  
  
The Ferrari 166 MM was designed for long-distance racing events such as the Mille Miglia, from which the “MM” designation originates and as a tribute to its predecessor, the “166 Sport”. The Ferrari 166 MM was also called “Barchetta”, a reference to the car’s body shape, which is reminiscent of a small boat (*barchetta* in Italian).  
  
Beyond its extraordinary history as a race car, this Ferrari, with chassis number #0056M and equipped with the iconic V12 engine developed by Gioacchino Colombo, is also the first Ferrari to arrive in Portugal, which it did on 10 June 1950.  
  
This model began its extensive participation in Portuguese competitions driven by Guilherme Guimarães at the 1st Portuguese Grand Prix, held on 17 June 1951 in Boavista, Porto. It then raced in the 10th Vila Real International Circuit, again piloted by Guimarães, qualifying 8th on the grid among 17 competitors. Unfortunately, the car did not finish either race due to mechanical issues.  
  
The following day, the 166 MM competed in the Lima Porto Stadium’s Nocturnal Festival, driven by Piero Carini, who borrowed the car from Guimarães. It achieved second place overall, with Giovanni Bracco taking the victory.  
  
This Ferrari 166 MM Barchetta Touring also participated in the 2nd Portuguese Grand Prix, finishing 8th overall, and in the 11th Vila Real International Circuit on 6 July, where it placed fifth. It also competed in the Rampa da Penha in Guimarães, among many other events.  
  
However, its racing career extended beyond Portugal. In 1957, the car was sold to the Automóvel e Touring Clube de Angola (ATCA) to be used in competitions with drivers selected by the club.  
  
Driven by Maximino Morais Correia, it took part in the 1st Angola Grand Prix in September 1957 but failed to qualify for the race due to several mechanical issues. Nevertheless, in September of the following year, it raced in the 2nd Luanda City Cup, finishing 6th overall.  
  
The car also competed in the 3rd Leopoldville Grand Prix in the Belgian Congo and the 3rd Angola Grand Prix. In July 1960, João Alves drove the 166 MM in the Lourenço Marques City Cup in Mozambique, finishing 7th overall in a race won by Syd van der Vyver.  
  
In the same year, ATCA sold the 166 MM to António Lopes Rodrigues, who registered it in Mozambique and subsequently entered it in the Rampa da Polana, Lourenço Marques.  
  
In August 1963, the car changed hands again, being sold to Hugh Gearing from Johannesburg, South Africa.  
  
Ten years later, in 1973, Gearing sold it to Robert van Zyl, also from Johannesburg. Robert and Geerie van Zyl participated in the Historic Mille Miglia from 9 to 12 May 1996. The following year, Robert attended the South African Ferrari Club event celebrating Ferrari’s 50th Anniversary at the Kyalami circuit.  
  
Robert and Patricia van Zyl drove the Ferrari again in the Historic Mille Miglia in May 2004 and repeated the feat in May 2011.  
  
Later that year, on 17 September, Geerie van Zyl raced the 166 MM in the Freddie March Memorial Trophy, part of the Goodwood Revival Meeting.

3007fb96-e72b-5a22-9b88-e468d7089d54.name: Chrysler Series 75 Tonnuau Phaeton

3014d292-46d6-5552-8846-8782d58e0b90.name: Foot reliquary
3014d292-46d6-5552-8846-8782d58e0b90.description: When Basel split into two half-cantons in 1833, the famous Basel Minster Treasure suffered the same fate. The new Canton Basel-Landschaft received 64 per cent of the treasure, but because it was desperately short of funds, it converted the ecclesiastical riches into cash, among them the silver reliquary of 1450, which brought the exchequer 562 francs. The reliquary has the shape of a foot, consistent with its contents – allegedly the foot bones of a young boy who was murdered in Bethlehem on Herod’s command. What chills modern viewers to the bone today, used to be the object of religious devotion to many. Through a of rock glass opening believers could catch a glimpse of the sacred relic and hope for divine assistance.

30f8c92a-d056-538d-835c-8f96181283c0.name: Ikhdari Dress (*Malaq*)
30f8c92a-d056-538d-835c-8f96181283c0.description: This *malaq* dress originates in the Al-Khadir area of Bethlehem District, where women embroider it by hand. It is worn only by brides for their wedding day. This dress is made with *Abu Warda* fabric. It has a traditional *malaq* chest panel of flower pot motifs, bordered by two pieces of blue velvet fabric with a bird embroidered on them. The neck and shoulders are made of red fabric. The sleeves are made with silk *hirmizi* cloth in addition to the original fabric of the dress and are embroidered with a Bethlehem clock and a bird. The *banayeq* (side panels) are embroidered with clock and floral motifs in addition to multiple crosses. Traditional Palestinian costumes are characterized by strong emphasis on decoration and colour and are designed from the finest and most expensive fabrics, as shown by this dress.

32a93df9-c069-57e3-b628-2bc42052e740.name: Lancia D50
32a93df9-c069-57e3-b628-2bc42052e740.description: Two fuel tanks mounted outside the bodywork, separately from the body of the car, are among the special features of this car; these were put in place as designer Vittorio Jano wanted to achieve good aerodynamic profiling. It made its racing debut at the 1954 Spanish Grand Prix, with Alberto Ascari at the wheel, fresh from a one-year contract with Lancia. The first victory came with Ascari at the 1955 Turin Grand Prix and then at the Naples Grand Prix in the same year. Further accolades would follow: Juan Manuel Fangio drove the D50 to his championship at the 1956 Formula 1 race. This model can travel at 280km/h thanks to its eight-cylinder V-shaped engine, which provides 260 horsepower at 8,000 revolutions per minute and displaces 2,488 cubic centimetres.

32de395b-4ca1-577b-a6cd-5f3baac701da.name: Chrysler Windsor Deluxe
32de395b-4ca1-577b-a6cd-5f3baac701da.description:
This black-lacquered car is viewed as iconic in Chrysler history. Produced between 1939 and the 1960s, the Chrysler Windsor fulfilled each and every desire of Americans after the second world war.  
  
As a more luxurious model compared to the New Yorker, this full-sized sedan from 1951 embraced the changing times with a redesign. The cigarette lighter, map lights and safety-padded dashboard would breathe new life into the steadfast car.  
  
With great popularity among political leaders and celebrities, this model belongs to the state cars owned by the third ruler of Qatar, Sheikh Abdullah Bin Jassim Al Thani. While the fashionable fins endured as a lasting feature, the Windsor remains a remarkable car in collections beyond the United States.

33ed9dae-cbca-529d-b595-f5e9b3bc4791.name: Sunbeam Grand Prix
33ed9dae-cbca-529d-b595-f5e9b3bc4791.description: In 1923, Sunbeam boss Louis Coatalen recruited the renowned Fiat engineers Bertarione and Becchia. They developed three cars for the 1924 Lyon Grand Prix, including this highly original No. 3. The No. 3 features two overhead camshafts, a roller crankshaft, a Rootes compressor, a dry sump, four-wheel servo brakes and a low-slung chassis. Although it failed to win in the 1924 Grand Prix de l'A.C.F, the two-litre Sunbeam has to its credit a very long line of successes in all kinds of events, including Grands Prix, world and class records and hill climbs.

344b5052-d321-5831-905e-01ed9243f962.name: Renault 16 TX
344b5052-d321-5831-905e-01ed9243f962.description: When it was released in 1965, the R16 revolutionized the world of sedans with its two-volume five-door body and a rear hatch. The original design is due to Philippe Charbonnaux, who created the first style office at Renault in 1960 with the release of the R8. The first model was followed in 1973 by the TS and in 1976 by the TX with five-speed gearbox, four iodine headlights, rear wiper, centrally locking doors, etc. The R16 remained in production from 1965 to 1980, resulting in 1,851,502 cars produced.

34773d1c-926e-5cef-b3aa-43c643a278b5.name: Alfa Romeo 2600 Sprint Zagato
34773d1c-926e-5cef-b3aa-43c643a278b5.description: Introduced in 1961, the Alfa Romeo 2600 was the top-of-the-range model, available at the time in Sedan, Sprint (coupe designed by Bertone) and Spider (Touring) versions. They had a new in-line six-cylinder engine with twin camshafts. Zagato presented their vision of the 2600 Coupe at the end of 1962. This prototype featured completely innovative lines compared to Alfa Romeo's offering. The final version of 1965 was not unlike the Lancia Flaminia Sport Zagato, presented a few years earlier. Despite good performance and Zagato's signature, production of the model remained confidential: from 1965 to 1967, only 105 examples were produced.

35a55142-cbad-545f-9150-ff76ab018f9b.name: The Archangel Gabriel
35a55142-cbad-545f-9150-ff76ab018f9b.description: This icon depicts the Archangel Gabriel turned to the left, indicating that it comes from the Deesis tier of an iconostasis. He wears the *alb* (tunic) of a deacon and the liturgical coat of a bishop. In his right hand, he holds a sphere of light and in his left hand, a rod. The Archangel Gabriel, whose name means “man of God” in Hebrew, has been called the leader of the heavenly hosts. He is associated with numerous biblical events, including the announcements of the births of Mary and John the Baptist, and most importantly, the Annunciation, in which Gabriel proclaimed to the Virgin Mary that she would conceive and bear a son named Jesus.

37c5135b-e0b0-5712-87f7-50aa9365f54f.name: Bugatti Type 35B
37c5135b-e0b0-5712-87f7-50aa9365f54f.description:
The ascendance of the Type 35 coincided with the golden age for Ettore Bugatti's eponymous Bugatti brand. The much-famed Type 35 achieved over two thousand victories in competition for the Molsheim marque. Those wins came on both the humblest and the most prestigious of theatres – including the 1924 French Grand Prix held in Lyon.  
Interestingly, though the Bugatti Type 35 featured extraordinary lines, it was still considered modest compared to those of the short-lived Type 32 with its unusual wheel-enveloping sculpture. The elegance of the 35 was in the way the bonnet silhouette flowed from the radiator grille in the shape of a horseshoe, extending to a tapered rear end where the fuel tank sat. The Type 35 design had many an exceptional but quiet detail, such as its aluminum wheels – an absolute novelty at a time when the same material was only commonly used for bodywork. And unseen under that body was the new chassis, which incorporated curved stringers that provided strength and rigidity for the lightweight body. The Type 35B on display in the Museu do Caramulo has been Portuguese from birth. Commissioned by Henrique Leherfeld, a Bugatti racer, it was christened with chassis number 4952 and engine 209 TC. The car was delivered to Leherfeld in July of 1930 and on 4 August, with him at the wheel, it won the Quilómetro do Setúbal. Continuing with a win at the 1930 Quilómetro do Mindelo with the dizzying average speed of 194km/h, the car remained at the top echelons of Portuguese competition for a further five years.  
  
In 1931, Lehefeld took part in the Rampa da Rebassada in Barcelona ​​where he finished third and followed up with a fifth-place finish in the Grand Prix de la Baule in France. Then in 1933, with Henrique Leherfeld once again behind the wheel, the car achieved two second-places finishes at the Campo Grande Circuit and the Boavista Circuit, also winning the October Cabo da Roca Hillclimb in the same year.  
  
By July of 1934, António Guedes Herédia had convinced Leherfeld to lend him the 35B for a race at the Vila Real Circuit. In a demonstration of immense class and virtuosity at the wheel, Herédia completely demolished the competition. The following year, Leherfeld took his Bugatti to Brazil, competing at the Circuito da Gávea and did exceptionally well to finish in second place. He returned to Brazil in 1936 but was less successful.  
  
A sixth-place finish in the 1937 Vila Real race was the last outing for this symbolic Bugatti, which in 1956, was acquired by João de Lacerda to become part of the Museu do Caramulo’s automobile collection. Given the pedigree of this Bugatti (and also being one of the most original in the world), the museum does not prevent it from being used frequently in national and international demonstrations.

3834cd40-a7ce-54ea-88cc-c3b62c548bc2.name: Mercedes-Benz 300 SL
3834cd40-a7ce-54ea-88cc-c3b62c548bc2.description:
Mercedes-Benz had a crisis on its hands following the Second World War. Its automobile range was aging and its manufacturing plants had been destroyed. The company’s chances of renewing its pre-war technological dominance were in serious jeopardy. The first post-war Mercedes-Benz was a renovated 170S which was unveiled at the Hanover Fair in May 1949. Two years later, at the 1951 Frankfurt Motor Show, Mercedes-Benz presented the 220 and 300 models – the main innovation of which was the new six-cylinder engine with an overhead camshaft.  
  
Using the new 1951 six-cylinder engine as a basis for inspiration, and with iron-clad determination, the brand set to work to recover its previous fame. Within the space of four years and at the 1954 Geneva Motor Show Mercedes-Benz unveiled one of the most revolutionary sports cars of all time: the 300 SL.  
  
Almost unheard of for a true sports car, the 300 SL managed to sell one thousand units by 1955 – only one year into its commercial production. Sales of the Mercedes-Benz super sports car also went quite well in Portugal, with the German brand selling 18 cars between February 1955 and December 1959. Many of them were destined for competition. Although the 300 SL was, first and foremost a car for everyday use, it was nevertheless fundamentally a strong competition car. This was proven when the competition model won the 1952 edition of the 24 Hours of Le Mans in the hands of Hermann Lang and Fritz Rieb, and also the Carrera Panamericana, with Karl Kling at the wheel.  
  
The car’s success started with the engine, internally named the M194, which was worked on by the brand’s competition department and equipped with the latest Bosch fuel injection. The engine installation was initially too high and affected the centre of gravity of the car. To get around this problem, Mercedes engineers laid the engine at a 50-degree angle and fitted it with a dry-sump system. This modification earned the engine the nickname “Schräge Otto”, which means “Otto lying down” in English, alluding to Markus Otto, the inventor of the four-stroke internal combustion cycle.  
  
The world’s press at the time were impressed by the innovative solutions used in the construction of the 300 SL chassis. Inspired by some aeronautical designs, engineers at Mercedes-Benz designed the new sports car with a tubular chassis, consisting of a triangulation of tubes that served as support structures for the mechanical components and bodywork.  
  
One of the most iconic features on the 300SL is the upwards-opening doors. This was necessary due to the excessive height of the chassis at the sides, preventing the use of traditional door mechanisms. The 300 SL immediately became known in Germany as the Flügelturen ("wing doors"), in England as the Gullwing and in France the Papillon ("butterfly").  
  
At the beginning of series production, the 300 SL, Mercedes-Benz model W194, could be ordered with several final transmission ratios, and with varying maximum speeds determined by the gearing. With the 3.42:1 ratio, the car reached a speed of 254km/h in fourth gear, while for the longest gearing ratio of 3.25:1, the top speed was 267km/h. The first cars tested by journalists were equipped with a final ratio of 3.64:1, providing a lesser top speed of 217km/h.  
  
The benefit of the lower top speed was that acceleration from 0 to 100km/h took just eight seconds. All of these figures become even more impressive when we consider that the 300 SL weighed 1233kg and was capable of very reasonable fuel consumption of around 15.6 litres for every 100km travelled.  
  
The brand’s experience in competition allowed it to fit the coupe with suspension geometries very similar to those seen on the track – although in the wrong hands this impacted the car’s drivability. At the rear, Mercedes-Benz equipped the SL with a swing-arm geometry which had a central pivot that, in the hands of experienced drivers, allowed the 300 SL to deliver fabulous performance but, in less experienced hands, made the car difficult to drive.

3973041d-53a7-5230-aa77-351da8676009.name: Lamborghini Miura P400 SV
3973041d-53a7-5230-aa77-351da8676009.description:
Although the main highlight of the Miura, which debuted in the 1965 Turin motor show, was its body and performance figures, the use of a mid-mounted engine was a game-changer for road-going supercars. The solution was suggested to Ferruccio Lamborghini by Gian Paolo Dallara, the then director of the brand’s engineering department, who wanted to manufacture a racing car.  
  
The first Lamborghini Miura, designated the P400, had a 60-degree V12 engine made entirely of aluminum. The 3929cc unit had four overhead camshafts and four triple-body Weber 46IDA 3C1 carburetors could reach 350hp at 7000 revolutions per minute.  
  
The transmission was a fully synchronised five-speed gearbox with a ZF self-locking differential. The wishbone suspension, also derived from competition, was independent on all four wheels along with helical springs, telescopic dampers and torsion bars.  
  
The first Miura was able to reach a top speed of 273km/h, taking 4.9 seconds to reach 100km/h and 11.7 seconds to reach 160km/h.  
  
Over the years, the Lamborghini Miura has benefited from some improvements, mainly on the engine, which helped it become more powerful. Lamborghini also improved the build quality, which increased somewhat the total weight of the car.  
  
In 1969 the Miura P400 S appeared equipped with four triple-body Weber 40IDL 3L carburetors and a changed compression ratio to 10.7:1, previously only 9.5:1. The V12 engine developed 370hp at 7700 revolutions per minute, and although the car saw its weight rise considerably, the performance remained phenomenal. The top speed was now 277km/h, taking just six seconds to reach 100km/h and 15 seconds to reach 160km/h.  
  
The Lamborghini Miura achieved instant fame, being one of the most coveted sports cars at the time, even though its production numbers were never truly big. Lamborghini produced 474 units of the P400 (1966–69), while for the P400 S, the second series (1969–71), only 140 units were produced. The last and most desired series was the P400 SV Miura (1971–72). Only 150 units of those were produced.  
  
This latest evolution saw the power of its engine increase to 385hp at 7700 revolutions per minute, allowing a maximum speed of 290km/h. In addition, it was much better behaved on the road and more reliable.  
  
The Miura continued to change according to the world of competition, such as the addition of a separate lubrication system for the engine and gearbox. The self-locking differential was another of the improvements, as was the completely revised suspension, which now worked in conjunction with the wider rear tyres. The wider tyres also forced Lamborghini to widen the body. The interior too received some attention, such as the addition of leather trim.  
  
The fabulous Lamborghini P400 SV Miura in the Museu do Caramulo rolled out of the Sant’Agata factory on 22 April 1971, as part of the final series of this supercar. In 1985, it returned to the Italian factory again to be completely overhauled, painted and reupholstered, leaving it in perfect condition.

399d3607-1f8f-5427-822a-f2ac90de3a10.name: Alfa Romeo 1900 SSC
399d3607-1f8f-5427-822a-f2ac90de3a10.description:
Designed by Orazio Satta, the stunning new Alfa Romeo 1900 turned a lot of heads at the 1950 Paris Motor Show. It was also the first Alfa to be manufactured on a production line by the Italian marque following a restructure aimed at making the company self-sufficient. As a testament to its quality, the car remained in production until 1959. Available in two- and four-door versions, the new 1900 was proffered as the “family car that won races at the weekend”, a fact proven by the car’s successes on esteemed stages like the Targa Florio and the Stella Alpina.  
  
In 1951 the short wheelbase version of the Alfa Romeo 1900 appeared, and it was immediately embraced as the standard-bearer by the Italian body-stylists of the time. From Pininfarina to Zagato, Ghia, Castagna and Boano, the new 1900C would receive new forms that tried to accentuate its sporting spirit. But it would be Carrozzeria Touring Superleggera, a company founded in the late 1920s, that produced the largest number of 1900C’s. Always linked to the Arese brand, Touring offered at the time four different types of bodies for the 1900s. Out of those, the Superleggera was the most coveted because of its light weight and elegance. Using a patented construction system based on a thin steel tubing structure lined with hand-tapped panels, the Alfa Romeo 1900C SS was as ingenious as it was fast, making it a popular choice for private individuals with aspirations in the world of motor racing.  
  
The magnificent Alfa Romeo 1900C SS in the Museu do Caramulo was first registered in 1956, a year after the model was introduced. Its 1975cc four-cylinder engine outputs 115hp, which is delivered to the road through a five-speed fully synchronized gearbox. With its black lacquered Touring Superleggera body, light tinted interior and spoked Borrani rims, the 1900C SS with license plate HC-64-82 is one of the most exquisite examples still in existence.  
  
Interestingly, this very car, donated by Vicente Cannas Mendes and housed in the museum, is fully eligible to participate in the Mille Miglia.

39c77b9c-54ff-5cb2-bbbc-c8a5ef99dbc2.name: Set of Icons from a Festival Tier
39c77b9c-54ff-5cb2-bbbc-c8a5ef99dbc2.description:
This set of 12 icons, the only one of its kind in the United States, is believed to be from the Pskov region of Russia. The icons were originally hung on the festival tier of an iconostasis, the partition separating the nave from the sanctuary of an Orthodox church. The festival tier highlights the major holidays of the Orthodox liturgical calendar. This set includes the following images:  
  
1\. The Meeting of Anna and Joachim  
2\. The Nativity of the Virgin Mary  
3\. The Nativity of Christ  
4\. The Presentation of Christ  
5\. The Transfiguration  
6\. The Raising of Lazarus  
7\. The Crucifixion  
8\. The Three Marys at the Sepulchre  
9\. The Descent  
10\. The Ascension of Christ  
11\. The Holy Trinity  
12\. The Feast of Pentecost

3a71d542-5e72-54c9-808c-51df8069dd8b.name: Ikhdari Dress (*Malaq*)
3a71d542-5e72-54c9-808c-51df8069dd8b.description: *Malaq* dress made of *Abu Warda* fabric and *Ikhdari* fabric with green, burgundy, orange and black stripes. The dress has a chest panel embroidered with the image of a vase (the traditional chest panel of a *malaq* garment) and is adorned with two pieces of blue velvet embroidered with a bird. The sleeves are wide, made of *Hormozi* silk fabric, with an *Al-Talhami* clock shape and embellished with a bird motif. Embroidery on the chest panel resembles the traditional stitch of *malaq* dress with floral motifs, while the collar on the neck and shoulders is made with pink cloth and connected to the chest panel by a line of russet velveteen trim. The front of the dress shows the original fabric colors without embroidery, while the back panel shows four horizontal stripes of the fabric. The *banayeq* (side panels) are of silk cloth and are connected to the dress by *manajel* (thick braid work connecting the dress parts). The bottom sections of the *banayeq* are adorned with simple floral motif embroidery and some crosses. This dress is worn by women for weddings and other special occasions.

3a80e4c4-026d-52d0-9bf9-a73dd5af2656.name: Citroën DS 21
3a80e4c4-026d-52d0-9bf9-a73dd5af2656.description: After the success of the Traction Avant and the groundbreaking 2CV, Citroën outdid itself with the DS. Apart from its exceptionally comfortable suspension, the car’s underlying technology was not particularly extraordinary. However, Italian designer Flaminio Bertoni had mastered his craft to such an extent that he created a true revolution. The DS’s sophisticated styling and engineering sent shockwaves through the automotive world, with even luxury brands panicking as Citroën offered such refinement at highly competitive prices. Thankfully for them, the DS remained an outlier; even 60 years later, no one has managed to replicate Bertoni’s masterpiece. To this day, nearly all car designers regard the DS as their greatest source of inspiration, and museums are eager to display it as an iconic design piece.

keywords: Hydropneumatic suspension; futuristic design; fiberglass roof; innovation

3a9f9dea-210a-5f6b-8b09-dc7612ae85eb.name: Dodge Power Wagon
3a9f9dea-210a-5f6b-8b09-dc7612ae85eb.description:
This all-American truck stands out in Sheikh Faisal’s collection, having been passed down from his father Sheikh Qassim bin Faisal Al Thani. A trailer-unit, rope, and replacement tire equip the red Dodge Power-Wagon to surf along the desert dunes with ease.  
  
Out of the desire to teach the art of driving, Sheikh Faisal built a replica of the truck, which sits next to the original. Sheikh Faisal’s children would practice across Al Samriya estate with their father as their instructor.  
  
The Oryx antlers crown the front as reminders of the wagon’s past life in hunting activities with falcons. Today, a flair of nostalgia surrounds American trucks as Qataris associate these vehicles with the trodden local landscape.

3bc61cff-a133-5a4c-8c91-17c972723305.name: Winston Churchill waving his hat atop his walking stick in front of the Zunfthaus zur Meisen
3bc61cff-a133-5a4c-8c91-17c972723305.description:
Winston Churchill waves to a cheering crowd packed into the cathedral square in Zurich after giving a speech on 19 January 1946. Churchill visited Switzerland again from 23 August to 20 September 1946 when he travelled from Geneva via Lausanne and Bern to Zurich where he gave his famous speech on Europe at the University of Zurich. Although by then he was leader of the opposition, and was on a private visit to Switzerland, Churchill received an enthusiastic welcome befitting a statesman.  
Everywhere he went, photographers treated Churchill’s trip through Switzerland like a state visit. The Presse Diffusion Lausanne (PDL) agency covered his visits to Lausanne and Zurich. The Swiss National Museum acquired the archives of PDL and Actualités Suisses Lausanne (ASL) in 2007. Combined they number around six million images in the form of negatives, prints, and slides. Covering the years from 1937 to 1999, they record the most significant developments during the era of analogue press photography.

3cebc4da-cf91-5a75-a8f2-f8a6d99fcc59.name: Buick 8 Special
3cebc4da-cf91-5a75-a8f2-f8a6d99fcc59.description:
Recognisable by the “Special” inscription on the front fenders, this deluxe Buick model prioritises passenger comfort over speed.  
  
Despite the emphasis on cosiness with plush interiors, the “straight-eight engine” achieves 120 horsepower. This 1940 sedan represents the third generation of “Fireball Eights” with a new post-war design, a dramatic grille, and the Dynaflow automatic transmission.  
  
While a best-seller in the US, this car would witness defining moments in Qatar and America.

3ea1769e-eb4a-5f18-8549-2c33b4e49a46.description:
The 1961 190 SL Mercedes impresses visitors with its custom blue paint. The luxury roadster remained in production from 1955 until 1963, unveiled at the New York Auto Show.

45d767b4-fcfa-5a22-97f1-6135821c6624.name: Figure sleigh 'Triton'
45d767b4-fcfa-5a22-97f1-6135821c6624.description: The “Triton” sleigh at the Swiss National Museum is one of the most interesting and beautiful pieces of the respective collection. Built in the second half of the seventeenth century, it belonged to the family Pfyffer von Altishofen. The sculptures’ exquisite carvings are attributed to the artist Hans Wilhelm Tüfel (1631–1695) of Sursee. The style elements such as the dolphins’ open mouths, the “Triton”, and the fish on the runners were inspired by the Fontana del Tritone at Piazza Barberini in Rome. The Pfyffer family had close ties to Rome, given that, over the course of time, eleven family members served as commanders of the Swiss Papal Guard. Special features of the sleigh include that it could be drawn by either one or two horses and that the large open shell provided space for two passengers apart from the driver who sat on a special platform at the back. Showpiece sleighs like this were used primarily by the nobility for their pleasure outings through the snowy winter landscape and during carnival. The sleigh was donated to the museum by a wealthy brewer from Zofingen in 1934 and now presents itself again in its original splendour.
45d767b4-fcfa-5a22-97f1-6135821c6624.method_for_datation: The carvings were attributed to Hans Wilhelm Tüfel, who lived in Sursee.

475e49ee-eb2e-5fd2-a068-1be681fa5929.name: Mercenary’s helmet
475e49ee-eb2e-5fd2-a068-1be681fa5929.description: It began when a farmer in the canton of Ticino found an old gravestone in 1900. Soon it became clear that what lay buried there was not just a collection of old bones. In fact, there were over 500 such graves, all dating from the Iron Age. About one-fifth of the burials were warriors who had been interred with their lances, shields, swords, and helmets.The Roman Empire had taken to hiring mercenaries to aid its expansion to the north towards the end of the Iron Age. Mercenaries used their own weapons and armour, and the helmet found in the grave has been identified as belonging to a mercenary who came from the Central Alps. The mercenaries would return to their homes after completing their period of service. When they died, they were given a warrior’s funeral as befitted their status, like this man from Giubiasco, whose origins are revealed by the shape of his helmet. It’s all in the shape. Even in archaeology.

47cae498-46b8-572c-ad1b-8bf21213c49a.name: Mercedes-Benz 770 *Grosser*
47cae498-46b8-572c-ad1b-8bf21213c49a.description:
When Mercedes-Benz introduced the new 700 (codenamed the W07) in 1930, it had one thing in mind – to be the vehicle of choice for sovereigns and heads of states. Being the largest and most expensive Mercedes-Benz, only 117 units were produced from 1930 to 1938 in their Untertürkheim factory. The armoured Pullmann limousine accounted for 42 of these units. Emperor Hiroito of Japan acquired three of them, and two came to Portugal in 1938. Once there, one of the 770s famously belonged to Portuguese head of state Prof. António de Oliveira Salazar, having been one of several armoured models acquired for him. The history of armoured vehicles acquired in the name of Oliveira Salazar, then President of the Council of Ministers, forms one of the most curious chapters in Portugal’s history.  
  
After the failed bombing attempt on Sunday, 4 July 1937 on Avenida Barbosa du Bocage, when Salazar was on his way to morning Mass, the State Surveillance and Defense Police (PVDE) ordered two Type 770 Pullmansteel in October of that year. The order was made through the Mercedes-Benz agent in Lisbon, Sociedade Comercial Mattos Tavares, Lda, but given the specificity of the model, they transferred the order to the brand’s offices in Germany.  
  
According to the factory files, both chassis were completed on 18 January 1938 and the Pullmansteel bodies on 9 March. Both cars were then shipped to Lisbon on 12 April. They were registered in June 1938, in the name of PVDE, and were immediately made available to the Presidents of the Republic and the Council, General Óscar Carmona (AL-10-71, chassis # 182 067) and Prof. Oliveira Salazar (DA-10-72, chassis # 182 066).  
  
Salazar, who had not been consulted on the purchase of the cars, soon expressed his discontent, refusing to use the Mercedes-Benz assigned to him. This was not only because it was an ostentatious car, but also because it was thought to have been a gift from Hitler to the President of the Council. The car was used only once – on the occasion of the official visit of Generalissimo Franco in 1949. The car’s scant usage was by driver Raúl to transport visitors to and from Palacete de São Bento. Because of this, the odometer read only 6,000 kilometres when, seventeen years later, it was sold at a public auction by the Directorate-General for Finance.  
  
The auction was won after six counts by the scrap dealer Alfredo Nunes, who registered it in his name on 9 February 1955. It was sold shortly afterward to the Beato and Olivais Voluntary Firefighters to be used as their ambulance. The conversion costs however proved much too high, and they sold it on 16 June 1956 to João de Lacerda, to be displayed in the Museu do Caramulo.  
  
Nowadays, the car, having circulated since 1956, has clocked up 12,949 kilometres, most of which have been in Caramulo – to and from the maintenance garage. There was never a need to restore the car because from paintwork to chrome and upholstery, it is impeccable. Even the Buna rubber tires are original, being maintained at 40 pounds of pressure so as not to cause cracks in the flanks.  
  
The 770 in the Museu do Caramulo is considered by experts to be the best-kept and most perfect Mercedes-Benz Grosser in the world.

4859e54f-5855-587b-935f-40a00ec2c500.name: The Mother of God Axion Estin
4859e54f-5855-587b-935f-40a00ec2c500.description:
These four icons form a set that depicts the Hymn of Axion Estin, as follows:  
  
It is truly meet and right to bless you, O Theotokos,  
Ever-blessed and most-pure mother of our God.  
More honorable than the Cherubim,  
And beyond compare more glorious than the Seraphim,  
Who without corruption gave birth to God the Word,  
True Theotokos, we magnify you.  
  
According to tradition, this hymn was revealed to an elder monk and his disciple before an icon of the Mother of God in the sanctuary of the main church of Karyes on Mount Athos. During an all-night vigil, they were joined by an unknown monk who called himself Gabriel. As he chanted an unfamiliar hymn, the icon of the Mother of God began to glow. The elder asked Gabriel to write down this hymn, so he inscribed the prayer with his finger on a roof tile “as if it were made of wax”. The tablet was sent to Constantinople, while the image was venerated as miracle-working. The revelation is commemorated on June 11, and the icon is celebrated on July 13.

4877109c-214e-5b3f-b4ad-bff53cb7641a.name: Guldiner issued by the City of Zurich
4877109c-214e-5b3f-b4ad-bff53cb7641a.description: This guldiner, or guldengroschen, from 1512 represents the first thaler coin minted by the City of Zurich. Its obverse depicts the city’s three patron saints Felix, Regula, and Exuperantius holding their severed heads. According to legend, the three of them were persecuted as members of the Theban Legion and executed at Zurich. After decapitation, they are said to have carried their heads for a distance of 40 ells before lying down for the last time. The reverse depicts two lions supporting the city’s double coat of arms; above them is seen the crowned imperial coat of arms encompassed by the emblems of the sixteen Zurich shires (Vogtei).

49f03f3b-5c62-50a6-af56-a99b7f0fe737.name: Niche tile with pair of lovers
49f03f3b-5c62-50a6-af56-a99b7f0fe737.description: The open-work niche tile with its green-glazed surface shows a pair of lovers in contemporary costume (Tracht). The young man with the curly hair is evidently a falconer, which indicates that the couple belongs to courtly society. The tile is one of the pottery masterpieces from 15th century Zurich. In addition to animal motifs and Christian symbols, courtly love of the late Middle Ages, with its main themes of love, faithfulness and adoration, was a popular topic. Hunting with falcons, a leisure pursuit exclusive to the nobility, also fell into this category and reflected the social status of the stove’s owner. Stove-tiles thus make an important contribution to cultural history and provide information on mediaeval costumes, hairstyles and accessories. Until the 16th century, potters did not sign their works. The names of many masters and the locations of the potteries are known thanks to documents and account books. In large towns such as Zurich and Basle, potters joined guilds.

4f180fa5-704f-5c7d-ae79-fb6f43f46920.name: Reverse glass painting: *Vulcan surprises Venus*
4f180fa5-704f-5c7d-ae79-fb6f43f46920.description: The reverse glass painting by the Zurich artist Hans Conrad Gyger depicts the dramatic moment when Vulcan, the god of fire, steps into the sleeping chamber and catches his wife Venus in the amorous embrace of Mars. From the clouds above the Olympian gods witness the divine adultery. The theme’s composition – otherwise rarely depicted in Swiss reverse glass painting – traces back to the Zurich artist Gotthard Ringgli who gave Gyger two sketches with detailed studies of the two lovers. Ringgli, in turn, was relying on a Dutch drawing as his template. Possibly the precious work was created as a wedding present, with the intention of reminding the future couple of conjugal fidelity. Who commissioned the work is not known. The signature of Hans Conrad Gyger on the dark chest in the foreground was only discovered in 1997 in the context of restoration work. Until then Gyger had been famous above all for his cartographic work and, according to Joachim Sandrat, for a special procedure he developed for decorating glass objects with oil paints. Using this technique he decorated pictures, drinking vessels and mirrors, gaining popularity well beyond Zurich, as far as Paris, Florence and Venice.

534635d7-08e8-5000-8573-5552a013b052.name: Mercedes-Benz 380K
534635d7-08e8-5000-8573-5552a013b052.description:
Mercedes-Benz introduced the W22 model, better known as the MB 380, at the 1933 Berlin motor show, one of the most important automobile events of the time. The German firm immediately captured the world’s attention with its new flagship car. Contrary to the naming system on the previous S-class models, the letter ‘K’ on the new models stood for "compressor" and not "short". Between 1933 and 1934, only 157 units of the 380K model were produced, the majority being Cabriolet types A, B and C. It was then succeeded by the 500K (W24), of which 342 units were produced, which was then finally succeeded by 419 units of the 540K (W29).  
There were only 44 units produced of the 380K type C with two doors, four seats and two side windows. Two arrived in Portugal in 1934. One of those was acquired by doctor Guilherme Pereira Caldas, who won the 1st Estoril Elegance Award in that year. The Museu do Caramulo is very proud to be in possession of such a rare specimen by the German manufacturer.  
  
The file for this vehicle is still kept by the Stuttgart factory, and it shows that the order of the vehicle was placed by Sociedade Comercial Mattos Tavares, Lda, a Mercedes agent in Lisbon. The car was shipped on 30 January 1934 and was duly received on March 24th of the same year.  
  
Purchased by João de Lacerda on 12 March 1956, thise 380K type C was fully rebuilt in the private workshop of Harry Rugeroni at Rua Tomás Ribeiro, Lisbon.

54677b11-d256-5fc3-8a09-c575b3c60376.name: Langenthal vase
54677b11-d256-5fc3-8a09-c575b3c60376.description: The amphora-shaped flower vase was produced in the porcelain factory of Langenthal (Canton of Bern) founded in 1906. The vase featuring large, stylized flowers with an Asian touch was hand-painted in 1924 by Fernand Renfer, the company’s artistic director. Its modernistic look is inspired by the style called Art Deco which spread from France in the wake of the famous Parisian Exposition internationale des Arts décoratifs et industriels modernes. Renfer’s entry into the Langenthal factory in 1920 marked the beginning of an extremely creative phase in the 1920s and 1930s with an output of top-quality and aesthetically highly appealing ware. During the same period the enterprise also joined the design association Swiss Werkbund and regularly employed artists as designers. The vase was part of a major private collection of early Langenthal porcelain, which the Swiss National Museum was able to acquire in 2007.

5c13ad64-b549-5470-8c28-60447c1829ab.name: Christ in Majesty
5c13ad64-b549-5470-8c28-60447c1829ab.description: This icon, known as Christ in Majesty, was once part of the Deesis tier as well as the centerpiece of an iconostasis, a wall of icons separating the nave from the sanctuary in an Orthodox church. An icon of the Mother of God would have hung to the right and an icon of John the Baptist to the left. The Deesis tier usually extends outward on either side with Archangels Michael and Gabriel and the apostles facing Christ. This image represents Christ’s Second Coming and Last Judgment. He is seated on a throne surrounded by seraphim and cherubim angels in a scene of glory based on visions of the Old Testament prophets. Christ’s radiance illuminates the whole scene. The corners depict the symbols of the four evangelists, Matthew, Mark, Luke and John. Christ bestows a blessing with his right hand and in his left holds the Bible open to the passage, “Come to me all ye that labor and are heavy laden and I will give you rest” (Matthew 11:28-29). The Greek letters in three sections of Christ’s halo represent the oneness of the three-part Trinity. At the very top of this icon are the letters IC and XC, representing the first and last initials of the Greek name for Jesus Christ.

5d81f529-0519-5b10-ba1c-6c8d92b01735.name: The Battle between the Novgorodians and the Suzdalians
5d81f529-0519-5b10-ba1c-6c8d92b01735.description: This icon type, among the first to depict an event from Russian history, illustrates the 1169 battle in which the Suzdalians besieged the city of Novgorod. During the siege, Archbishop Ilya of Novgorod ordered that an icon of the Mother of God be brought out from the Church of the Transfiguration to give the Novgorodians courage. According to legend, the icon was displayed on the city walls where it was struck by a Suzdalian arrow. The icon miraculously began to weep, and through the intercession of the Mother of God, the Novgorodians defeated the Suzdalians. This image is particularly rich in its narrative and compositional details.

615a7562-84b5-53a8-94c7-e0939cd2dc65.name: Perforated baton with incised wild horses
615a7562-84b5-53a8-94c7-e0939cd2dc65.description: 15,000 years ago, towards the end of the last Ice Age, human beings found an ideal campsite under a rock spur in Canton Schaffhausen. Here they ate, drank, worked flint stones, and did sewing work. The campsite was discovered in Herblingen, a district in the town of Schaffhausen, in the nineteenth century. Among the finds was a perforated baton made from reindeer antlers, featuring two incised wild horses. It is one of the oldest figurative representations ever found in Switzerland. It would be interesting to know what the baton was used for in the late Stone Age. Archaeologists assume that it served ritual purposes in connection with hunting. Drawing was considered a thaumaturgic act through which humans hoped to gain control over wild game and thus enhance their hunting luck.

63b3696e-c834-52f0-8e58-a0e0675d7445.name: Coune MG
63b3696e-c834-52f0-8e58-a0e0675d7445.description: In 1964, the Belgian coachbuilder Coune presented a coupé based on the new MGB. The car's design was clearly inspired by the Italian coachbuilders at that time: the rear section clearly resembled the Ferrari 275 GTB. This Coune MG was a great success: no less than 56 models of this fastback were produced, of which the first five were entirely out of steel. Following that, polyester was used for the roof and rear section, being simpler to produce and lighter.
63b3696e-c834-52f0-8e58-a0e0675d7445.author: Ahmed Chaouch

65a272ce-76ec-5d48-9b6b-0863deb47cbc.name: J.P.W. Prototype
65a272ce-76ec-5d48-9b6b-0863deb47cbc.description: Jean-Pierre Wimille was a renowned French racing driver. He won several Grand Prix races and triumphed at the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 1937 and 1939. After being part of the French Resistance during World War II, Wimille collaborated with engineer M. Viel to create this small post-war car. The design was drawn by Philippe Charbonneaux, while the body was constructed by Chapron on a tubular chassis with four independent wheels. The driver was positioned centrally, with space for one passenger on each side. The engine was centrally located at the rear. Its aerodynamic design, featuring a large plexiglass windshield and a small rear window, was particularly striking. The car on display is the first of three built between 1946 and 1948. Tragically, Wimille died in a crash in 1949 while driving a Simca-Gordini during practice for the Argentine Grand Prix.
65a272ce-76ec-5d48-9b6b-0863deb47cbc.author: Ahmed Chaouch
keywords: Experimental; post-war; steel construction; unique design

696eb90a-0ce9-5dba-973b-b54eeda3a5ad.name: Miniature Folding Iconostasis
696eb90a-0ce9-5dba-973b-b54eeda3a5ad.description: Miniature and folding iconostases were used starting in the 16th century, both by priests who traveled to rural areas and domestically by the Russian people. These icons, which vary in size and composition, are scaled-down versions of the partitions found in an Orthodox church and were largely used as a way to bring faith into the home. This icon consists of 15 parts and depicts the Deesis, festival and prophet tiers. The Mother of God is pictured in the center of the top row, flanked by unidentified saints.
696eb90a-0ce9-5dba-973b-b54eeda3a5ad.obtention: Purchased by Gordon Lankton from Simon Morsink, Amsterdam, in 2008. Gifted to the Museum of Russian Icons by Gordon Lankton in 2021.

6af07b8a-a412-5ec3-a872-6ecb7dc189c5.name: Disc fibula
6af07b8a-a412-5ec3-a872-6ecb7dc189c5.description: This brooch, called a fibula, belonged to a woman living in what is today the canton of Solothurn around the year AD 600. It is made of gold and set with semi-precious stones. The fibula was used to fasten a cloak over the wearer’s chest – a fashion the Germanic tribes had brought to Switzerland. The Germanic migration not only brought changes in fashion, customs, and diet to Switzerland, but also multilingualism. While the Alemannians imposed their own language on the north of the country, the Germanic tribes of the Langobards and Burgundians in the south and south-west adopted the Latin language of the local population. So it is thanks to the Germans that Switzerland is divided into German-speaking and Romance-speaking residents today.
keywords: Disc fibula; Early Middle Ages; Jewellery; Solothurn
materials: Filigree decoration, Inserts with semi-precious stones (garnet)

70acc160-3d11-54d7-ad72-3fbd51e11734.name: Alfa Romeo Disco Volante
70acc160-3d11-54d7-ad72-3fbd51e11734.description: Based on this experimental prototype, Alfa Romeo later built a dozen or so competition models with 2-, 3-, and 3.5-litre engines. One of these cars, a 6C 3000 CM, driven by Juan Manuel Fangio, finished second overall in the 1953 Mille Miglia. In a similar model Fangio also won the first Supercortemaggiore Grand Prix, held in Merano in the same year. The model donated to the Museum by Alfa Romeo in 1956 was built with a 2-litre engine and fitted with the powerful six-cylinder engine of the 6C 3000. This engine, with which the car can speed at 225km/h, displaces 3,495 cubic centimetres and provides 246 horsepower at 6,500 revolutions per minute.
