718b2755-b86b-5577-8fe4-dae39544ddbd.name: Scenes from the Life of John the Baptist
718b2755-b86b-5577-8fe4-dae39544ddbd.description:
John the Baptist was the cousin of Jesus Christ and preached in the Judean desert. He lived a life of self-denial by wearing camel hair clothing and eating only locusts and wild honey. The people of the region came to him to be baptized in the Jordan River. When Jesus asked to be baptized, John proclaimed that he was not worthy of such a task and that Christ should baptize him. Christ insisted, however, and during the baptism the Holy Spirit descended and a voice from heaven proclaimed, “This is my beloved Son in whom I am well pleased” (Matthew 3:17). John got into trouble when he criticized King Herod’s marriage to Herodias, who had a child from her previous marriage to Herod’s brother. Herod’s stepdaughter, Salome, convinced him to arrest John and demanded his head on a silver platter. Granting her wish, Herod ordered John beheaded.  
This icon shows several scenes from John the Baptist’s life in a single frame. At the top left, John is depicted in the wilderness, surrounded by animals. He receives inspiration from God in the form of flames. At the bottom, John is seen baptizing followers in the Jordan River while more followers prepare for baptism or don the white clothes of the newly baptized. In the top right corner of the icon, people stream out from the city while members of the aristocracy look on from above. The three figures in the central arch could be King Herod, his wife and stepdaughter, all of whom were responsible for John’s martyrdom.
718b2755-b86b-5577-8fe4-dae39544ddbd.obtention: Purchased by the Museum of Russian Icons from a private collection in 2010.

72a4f210-e9af-568c-82cb-538110bc11c0.name: City bus
72a4f210-e9af-568c-82cb-538110bc11c0.short_description: This bus was produced by the Gürel Toy Company in 1969, which was one of the most important tin toy manufacturers of the time. The company started manufacturing toys in 1944. The company is renowned for its huge variety of tin toys such as buses, planes, trucks, tanker trucks, vans, rattles, whistles, strollers, police cars, military vehicles and much more.

75647d49-efe8-541c-828b-b58acf35195a.name: God Rested on the Seventh Day
75647d49-efe8-541c-828b-b58acf35195a.description: In this icon, God reclines on a bed, illustrating the part of the creation story that reads, “On the seventh day He rested” (Genesis 2:2). Angels hold his bed and the temporarily vacant throne aloft while the Holy Spirit, represented by a dove, flies above them. All this takes place within a circle featuring the archangels, the evangelists, Christ and the Mother of God. Meanwhile, scenes from the rest of the creation story take place below. Labels on the back of this icon reveal that it was sold by Gimbels department store in the late 1930s, suggesting that it once belonged to William Randolph Hearst. Hearst was a newspaper entrepreneur who famously sold off large parts of his immense art collection during the Depression.
75647d49-efe8-541c-828b-b58acf35195a.obtention: Sold at "Exhibition of Russian Icons Arranged by Hammer Galleries", New York City, in 1937. Purchased by Gordon Lankton from Ikonen Galerie, Germany, in 2013. Gifted to the Museum of Russian Icons by Gordon Lankton in 2021.

7b36747d-dca7-598b-b985-ad4799a191fe.name: The Mother of God of the Burning Bush
7b36747d-dca7-598b-b985-ad4799a191fe.description:
The Mother of God is shown in the center of this icon surrounded by rays of light that extend outward to form an eight-pointed star. Angels, archangels and symbols of the evangelists are pictured both in and around the star. This icon is a reference to a passage from the book of Exodus in which Moses saw the burning bush unconsumed by fire. Moses and other prophets are often interpreted as foretelling the coming of Christ while the unburnt bush serves as a symbolic representation of the Virgin Mary.  
In this icon, the four evangelists are represented by four winged figures. The angel represents Saint Matthew, the lion stands for Saint John, the ox symbolizes Saint Luke and the eagle is associated with Saint Mark. These symbols are based on the biblical interpretations of Saint Irenaeus (130-202).
7b36747d-dca7-598b-b985-ad4799a191fe.obtention: Purchased by the Museum of Russian Icons from ArtVKG, New York City, in 2012.
keywords: Allegorical and symbolical figures; Virgin Mary and Child; Religious iconography; Angels

81099b4c-753f-53ba-9785-217e53613a49.name: Madonna and Child
81099b4c-753f-53ba-9785-217e53613a49.description: It was not roses that guarded the sleep of the enthroned Madonna with the Child, but human bones. And her sleep lasted not for a hundred years, but for several centuries. The sculpture was piously buried in the charnel house of the church of Raron according to a custom prevalent in Europe at the time, and gradually vanished beneath the skulls and bones of the dead. The reason for burying the wooden figure was provided by the rebuilding of the parish church between 1510 and 1515. The Romanesque Madonna had fallen out of fashion and was no longer needed. The person who finally kissed her awake again was not Prince Charming, but a tradesman from the canton of Valais. During restoration work on the charnel house of Raron in 1924, he was told to clear out the bones – and so he stumbled upon several sculptures, including the most significant example of Romanesque art in Switzerland.
keywords: Madonna; Child; Sculpture; Raron; Vallais
materials: Carved in the round, limewood, polychromy

81c6ce8f-139e-51e9-af11-99272504f19a.name: Porsche 911 SC Police
81c6ce8f-139e-51e9-af11-99272504f19a.description: In 1976, the Belgian Gendarmerie ordered twenty 911 Targa models with a narrow body but fitted with the hypermodern 210 hp Carrera RS- motor. Special equipment, apart from the flashing light and siren, included a CB- radio and a stop- signal. Owing to the car's power, the agents had to follow a special driving course, but that didn't prevent a few serious accidents. Only two of these cars are still registered today.
81c6ce8f-139e-51e9-af11-99272504f19a.author: Ahmed Chaouch

8295b2dc-f53b-5916-8630-8c3fce35e14c.name: Cadillac Series 62 *State Limousine*
8295b2dc-f53b-5916-8630-8c3fce35e14c.description: Ordered by the Belgian Royal Family and serving as an official parade car, this model has some unique features including the split front bench and a handle on the windscreen frame. It participated in most of the state occasions in the second half of the 1950s, such as the marriage of Prince Albert and Paola on 2 July 1959, but is especially famous as the wedding car of the royal couple Baudouin and Fabiola on 15 December 1960. For this occasion, a special plexi top was manufactured by coachbuilder Vesters & Neirinck of Brussels.

83383102-5642-59e4-b5c5-d35c70522e44.name: Gillet Sport *Tour du monde*
83383102-5642-59e4-b5c5-d35c70522e44.description: In 1927, aviation lieutenant Robert Fabry embarked on a perilous journey across the desert with this motorcycle, which could carry 350 kg of equipment. After travelling more than 20,000 km in 10 months, he arrived in Elisabethville. For more information, see the large panel.

8438c43b-63ab-580f-9b3a-31c91a430dd9.name: Itala 35/45 HP
8438c43b-63ab-580f-9b3a-31c91a430dd9.description: Itala’s prestige was such that it was one of the car manufacturers favoured by the Royal House of Savoy, in particular by Queen Margherita, for whom this 35/45 HP Itala was built. She christened it ‘Palombella’ and its refined bodywork was executed in Milan by Cesare Sala, one of the leading coachbuilders of the time. The chassis is identical to that of the famous Itala that won the Peking to Paris race in 1907, except for a few modifications. Note the silver eagle-shaped handles and the fold- down access ladder under the door in this luxurious ‘limousine landaulet’. The performance is almost identical to its racing predecessor: a four-cylinder engine, displacing 7,433 cubic centimetres, providing 45 horsepower at 1,250rpm, drives the car to reach 70km/h.

8485bf89-aab8-53ff-a59e-03b0ed9c4935.name: The Last Judgment
8485bf89-aab8-53ff-a59e-03b0ed9c4935.description: The Last Judgment is a common topic in Christian art. It combines biblical and apocryphal stories into a unified account of the end of times, of Christ coming to judge the world and of the afterlife. Typically, Russian Orthodox icons that depict the Last Judgment show Christ enthroned with a scale and an open Gospel. He is often flanked by the Virgin and Saint John the Baptist, who intercede for humankind. Adam and Eve are frequently seen kneeling at Christ’s feet. In Russian Orthodox iconography, the “serpent of suffering” is often depicted as well. Originally, the serpent was viewed as the instigator of original sin, seducer of Adam and Eve and the embodiment of evil. In this icon, 20 sins are depicted along the body of the snake in order of severity. They are as follows: (1) lying, (2) greed, (3) tale-telling, (4) idle talk, (5) anger, (6) blasphemy, (7) gluttony, (8) drunkenness, (9) slander, (10) foul language, (11) adultery, (12) fornication, (13) rape, (14) vanity, (15) money-mongering, (16) self-love, (17) despair, (18) murder, (19) self-glorification and (20) pride.
8485bf89-aab8-53ff-a59e-03b0ed9c4935.obtention: Purchased by Gordon Lankton from a private collection in 2006. Gifted to the Museum of Russian Icons by Gordon Lankton in 2013.

888a6e61-03f6-52c9-9f55-414d518e18b8.name: Altar panel with Mary Magdalene and John the Baptist
888a6e61-03f6-52c9-9f55-414d518e18b8.description: In the Middle Ages, lepers were segregated from the rest of society in lazarettos. In Zurich, these were located outside the city walls, close to running water, and had a chapel of their own. The St. Moritz lazaretto, which was built on the Spanweid in 1364, housed destitute lepers. The chapel received a new altarpiece in 1506. The inside of the panels depicts St. Mary Magdalene in costly fashionable clothing with a pouch and a cutlery holder. She is holding an open pot of ointment and promising the lepers hope of healing.
888a6e61-03f6-52c9-9f55-414d518e18b8.obtention: Permanent loan from the Zentralbibliothek Zurich as part of the «Morgengabe»
keywords: Painting; Chapel Spanweid; Zuerich; Mary Magdalene; John the Baptist; Zentralbibliothek;

89096e65-9786-5af7-b75c-3f4bf148072a.name: Darracq 12HP Open Tourer
89096e65-9786-5af7-b75c-3f4bf148072a.description: Alexandre Darracq began his storied career in the late 19th century with the manufacture of the successful Gladiator bicycles, which competed well in the French market of the 1890s. Dating from 1902, this car, sporting an Open Tourer bodywork, is one of the most important units of the Darracq brand. It was with this exact model that the French manufacturer launched himself properly into the automobile manufacturing scene. This extraordinary car is unique in the world: Its engine architecture has two separate cylinders which are connected in such a way that it appears as two single-cylinder engines.

89551a6b-2ae7-52e1-a91e-7ff3b1d265b5.name: Gradual
89551a6b-2ae7-52e1-a91e-7ff3b1d265b5.description: Some things are made to last forever. One of them is the Gradual from the St. Katharinental Abbey in what is today the canton of Thurgau. The late Gothic hymnal was created in 1312 and was used in the abbey for approximately 500 years. Because it was kept locked away between uses, the Gradual is in excellent condition and the colours of the precious miniatures adorning the pages have lost none of their brilliance. The book was opened only while the nuns sang from it during Mass. They would stand on the choir steps so that they could all read from the book at the same time. The name «Gradual» derives from the Latin word gradus meaning «step». The book is almost half a metre tall to enable all the nuns to read the liturgical chants. This Gradual is one of the most valuable manuscripts in Switzerland. Weighing thirteen kilograms, it is also a true heavyweight of cultural history.
89551a6b-2ae7-52e1-a91e-7ff3b1d265b5.owner: Swiss Confederation, Canton of Thurgau, Gottfried Keller Foundation

895f24e7-b822-5aa5-b3b1-241a91f0c94f.name: Ring ‘Potiential Diamond’
895f24e7-b822-5aa5-b3b1-241a91f0c94f.description: For his conceptual jewellery, Hans Stofer looks to everyday objects or nature – be it a light bulb, tinfoil, or a piece of coal. He combines them with precious stones or encloses them in wire mesh. There is always a hint of irony and humour about his pieces: his oversized ring made of a piece of coal in wire mesh, for instance, is called “Potential Diamond”. From 1972 to 1976, Hans Stofer was apprenticed as a precision instrument maker. Between 1981 and 1984, he attended the specialist jewellery and instrument-making class at the Zurich School of Design where, in 1985-86, he ran his own workshop before leaving for London in 1987. First, he taught metalwork at Camberwell College of Arts; in September 2006, he was appointed professor and head of Goldsmithing, Silversmithing, Metalwork, and Jewellery at the Royal College of Art.

89995be1-7027-55e0-b2ae-13f0acfa6847.name: Simca 1000 Rallye 2
89995be1-7027-55e0-b2ae-13f0acfa6847.description:
Like so many other models adapted from small SUVs, the history of the Simca 1000 Rallye 2 started with the very simple Simca 1000 and, starting in 1969, the Simca 1000 Spécial. Quite popular in the late ’60s, French-made cars began to be coveted for competing in sport classes reserved for small-engined cars. Responding to the market in 1970, the manufacturer brought out the Simca 1000 Rallye, equipped with a 1118cc 50hp engine.  
  
Simca again returned in September of 1972 with the 1000 Rallye 2. The Rallye 2’s four cylinders saw its displacement increased to 1294cc, and the power was increased to 82hp through the use of two double carburetors. Weighing a mere 860kg, the Rallye 2 reached 162km/h at top speed.  
  
Owner of an enviable record achieved on the national circuits, the Simca 1000 Rallye 2 in the Museu do Caramulo started its sports career in 1975 with Santinho Mendes at the wheel in the Rampa da Pena, where he came third in class. Mendes and the Simca would come home first in class at Estoril in the same year. Suffering a puncture, the car failed to finish again at Estoril on 27 July, driven this time by Jerónimo de Lacerda. But a month later, on 31 August 1975, at the Vila do Conde circuit with Lacerda at the helm, it very convincingly won its class – one of the car’s greatest achievements.  
  
Buoyed by the performance of the little Simca, the Caramulo driver set off to France to have the car prepared by the Simca Racing Team, in Lille. Still fresh from the trip and now with 86hp from the engine, the Simca was entered in the Estoril race, but Lacerda would be replaced by João Nabais, owing to poor health. A third in class finish was the reward for the factory-prepared Simca.  
  
Following the death of Jerónimo de Lacerda, his friend and well-known driver from the 1970s, Edgar Fortes, borrowed the Simca 1000 Rallye 2 from the new owner, António Adão, to secure two first places on the hills of Pena and Foia in 1978. The 1978 season would end with António Adão at the wheel of the Rallye 2 at the Estoril Circuit, the 500km of Estoril, the Rampa da Falperra and the Serra da Estrela Prize, where he had two fourth places in the first and third races.  
  
The car passed through the hands of Veloso Amaral, who raced it in the 1982 and 1983 seasons, competing in events such as the Vila do Conde Circuit and Rally de Portugal, though without the rigor and preparation that the car had previously enjoyed.  
  
After many years away from competition, the Simca 1000 Rallye 2 returned to Caramulo, where it was fully restored by João de Lacerda, son of Jerónimo de Lacerda, who revived the little Simca to its original specification, including the livery that was used by his father to win at the Vila do Conde Circuit in 1975.

8baacdf2-d985-5b5a-b5b5-818c598d2668.name: Lancia 037
8baacdf2-d985-5b5a-b5b5-818c598d2668.description:
The destiny at birth for the Lancia 037 was to be a replacement for the Fiat 131 Abarth, which was bowing out of competition after being crowned champion in 1980. Opinions were split within the Fiat Group as to which direction to go. Some in the company wanted to adapt an existing model, but these lost to a faction that wanted a car to be designed and built specifically for racing, as Fiat had done previously with the glorious Lancia Stratos.  
  
The project was developed as a collaboration between Lancia, Abarth and Pininfarina. They were tasked to design a car in accordance with the new FISA Regulations for Group B cars, requiring the production of 200 units of a road car, which bore a technical and styling specification that was very close to the racing version.  
  
Adoption of a turbocharged engine was initially considered, but Lancia was unable to develop and build one in the short time available. A four-wheel drive solution was also discarded, as the group preferred not to venture into complex technical solutions that could create regulatory breaches. The main ethos was to have a design that would be easy to repair mechanically and have parts that could be quickly changed on rallies.  
  
Even with the comparatively simple design, the 325hp rear-wheel drive Lancia triumphed over the world-famous Audi Quattro in the 1983 World Rally Championship. The championship win was in no small part aided by Abarth’s Volumex supercharger, which added between 0.60 and 0.90 bars of boost to the engine.  
  
Presented in its final trim at the 59th Turin Motor Show in 1982, the Lancia 037 immediately stole the show. Both journalists and brand enthusiasts flocked to see it.  
  
The 037 won six races in the WRC, clinching the title and ending a seven-year spell of failing to win the championship – the last such victory was with the Lancia Stratos.  
  
The Lancia 037’s participation in rallies ended tragically in 1985, when driver Attilio Bettega died in a crash on the Tour de Corse.

8c01ea8e-4a34-5b51-98ed-19f661cc145d.name: Monaco Trossi
8c01ea8e-4a34-5b51-98ed-19f661cc145d.description: The radial 16-cylinder engine, mounted at the front, solved cooling problem and at the same time determined the layout of the entire car. In fact, traction had to be at the front to avoid a overly long shaft as well as be able to exploit the grip of the front wheels. Unfortunately, this arrangement sealed the car’s fate. Due to the excess weight on the front drive wheels, the car was unstable even on the straight. It also oversteered when cornering, where it should have gained the most advantage. The car didn’t make it past the testing stages and thus remained just a futuristic prototype. This car can reach speeds of 200km/h; its engine displaces 3,982 cubic centimetres and provides 250 horsepower at 6,000 revolutions per minute.

8d033b2d-5baf-5699-a24f-6ac6be52e879.name: Centrepiece
8d033b2d-5baf-5699-a24f-6ac6be52e879.description: A native of Neuchâtel, Ernest Röthlisberger (1888–1964) was one of the most prolific goldsmiths working in art deco style during the 1920s and 1930s. A tea service he designed received an award at the 1925 International Exhibition of Modern Industrial and Decorative Arts. This large centrepiece is angular and geometric in form and was made with its ivory handles in 1929. An inscription on the underside reveals that this centrepiece was presented to an employee of the private bank Piguet et Cie in Yverdon-les-Bains in recognition of forty years of service.

8ecca203-295e-576b-be2c-1ce60f86ab0e.name: Erstfeld treasure
8ecca203-295e-576b-be2c-1ce60f86ab0e.description: The Erstfeld (UR) treasure is discovered by chance in a rock crevice in August 1962. The extraordinary assemblage is one of the most prominent masterpieces of Celtic goldsmithing. It consists of four torques and three arm rings made of high-carat gold (up to 95%) weighing 640 g in total. The rings are decorated with figural friezes, plant motifs and mythical creatures. One of the motifs shows the «Lord/Lady of the wild animals»: this deity is widely known, both in the Celtic tradition and in the mythology of the Mediterranean region.The gold rings are made in the 4th century BC in a workshop on the Swiss Plateau or in southern Germany. The gold treasure is quite probably a votive offering to a deity to ask for a safe crossing of the Alps.
keywords: archaeology; Erstfeld treasure; neck ring

8fee6c70-a79c-5c05-a2f3-7caec08b094a.name: Fiat 3½ HP
8fee6c70-a79c-5c05-a2f3-7caec08b094a.description: Fiat started mass production with the 3½ HP model, of which 30 were built. Developed by engineer Aristide Faccioli and derived from the Welleyes 3½ HP built by Giovanni Ceirano, the Fiat 3½ HP model was released a few months after the company was founded. The distinctive feature of this "little car" is the rear-mounted, twin-cylinder engine, water-cooled by way of a serpentine radiator, with three-speed gearbox without reverse and chain drive. Fuel consumption was about 8 litres per 100 km. The engine displaces 679 cubic centimetres and provides 4.2 horsepower at 800 revolutions per minute for a speed of 35km/h.

91edb81f-fd53-5ef4-97f9-e53eac5c04c2.name: Saint Nicholas of Mozhaisk with Scenes from His Life
91edb81f-fd53-5ef4-97f9-e53eac5c04c2.description: Saint Nicholas, a 4th-century bishop from modern-day Turkey, is one of the most venerated saints in Russia. Stories of Saint Nicholas giving gifts to the needy and protecting children spread far and wide as people traveled or emigrated from Russia to other countries. In this icon, a full-length statue of Saint Nicholas is set in a *kiot* (wooden box). Painted panels with images of Christ and the Mother of God were once affixed to either side. In the center panel, Saint Nicholas originally held a sword in his right hand and a church in his left hand; both are now missing. The doors are illustrated with important scenes from the saint’s life.

94f28839-f709-5cc7-bf4c-84a06693c6fe.name: Dust jacket; template for the edition of Heinrich Böll: *Ansichten eines Clowns*. Roman. dtv No. 400. Original drawing affixed to a pre-printed cover showing the title and publisher’s device
94f28839-f709-5cc7-bf4c-84a06693c6fe.description: Celestino Piatti (1922–2007) was one of the best-known graphic artists in Europe in the last third of the twentieth century. From 1961 to 1992, he designed the look of the Deutscher Taschenbuch Verlag (dtv). A whole generation of readers in German-speaking Europe associates works of world literature with the covers he designed for them. Piatti read all the books whose cover he designed, and confidently translated their key scenes into memorable images. The Swiss National Museum was able to acquire from the artist’s estate over 1,000 print templates, trial proofs, and cover designs produced for dtv.

9756abd9-b15c-5fd2-8268-42718f478e08.description:

Complete with a wooden exterior and manual horn, the T-Model revolutionised the car industry by becoming the first car with all its part manufactured by one company, Ford. Since 1919, the roadsters would also feature electric starters, although still thought of as being a decadent accessory.

97c84e4d-b5db-513a-8e7d-cfa06d0b62ff.name: In Thee Rejoiceth
97c84e4d-b5db-513a-8e7d-cfa06d0b62ff.description:
This icon is based on a famous hymn written by 7th-century saint and theologian, John of Damascus, to the Mother of God. The hymn includes the following text:  
  
All of Creation rejoices in thee, O full of grace:  
the angels in heaven and the race of men,  
O sanctified temple and spiritual paradise,  
the glory of virgins, of whom God was incarnate  
and became a child, our God before the ages.  
He made thy body into a throne,  
and thy womb more spacious than the heavens.  
All of creation rejoices in thee, O full of grace:  
Glory be to thee  
  
In this icon, the images of the Mother of God and Christ are serene while the choir of saints and people depicted at the lower part of this icon are animated and immersed in song. The landscape, with green trees on a white background, is symbolic of paradise. The crowd at the bottom of the image represents humankind, and the domes signify the church.

99cb3023-b001-53e7-abdf-540b59ee8ac4.name: Léon Bollée Voiturette
99cb3023-b001-53e7-abdf-540b59ee8ac4.description: Automaking was something of a Bollée family business: Léon's father and brother, both named Amédée, were renowned French pioneers of steam transmission. Starting in 1895 Léon built tricycles gave them the name of "voiturette", a name that later would become generic for small cars. This 3-wheeler was also popularly known as "la Tue Belle-mère" (mother-in-law murderer), because the passenger was seated up front. It has no suspension but is capable of reaching a potentially dangerous speed of 30km/h. The voiturette claimed first and second places in the first ever London-Brighton Run, in 1896. Notice the small steering wheel, an innovation at the time.
99cb3023-b001-53e7-abdf-540b59ee8ac4.author: Ahmed Chaouch

9a94a586-933d-570f-bdba-4376c9fd1357.name: Chests of drawers
9a94a586-933d-570f-bdba-4376c9fd1357.description: Chests of drawers emerged in the early 18th century and displaced chests as storage furniture. Baroque examples were decorated with lavish inlays of differently coloured types of wood. Typical of the French influence are the curved form, the lavish partially gilt brass mountings, and the marble top panel. The art workshop of the Funk brothers in Berne was the most important production site for luxury furniture in the 18th century. The style of the workshop was so unique that the name Funk-Möbel (Funk furniture) became a byword for form and quality.

9a9ecf47-bb64-514a-af2c-56b5ecf5fbac.name: Maserati 26B
9a9ecf47-bb64-514a-af2c-56b5ecf5fbac.description: This car features an eight-cylinder in-line engine, supercharged by a Roots compressor and double overhead camshaft timing system, with which Alfieri Maserati won third place overall at the 1927 Targa Florio. Even though Alfieri was forced to stop racing due to an accident at the Coppa di Messina, the 26 B had already won the favour of the drivers. Furthermore, in 1928 it won the prestigious Italian Makes Championship. According to the Maserati brothers, it was “the first car built in our workshops”. The engine displaces 1,980 cubic centimetres and provides 155 horsepower at 5,300 revolutions per minute. With it, the 26B can reach speeds of up to 180km/h.

9bc2393c-3ee9-5329-9801-b1c119d8e1b3.name: Benz 20HP Grand Landaulet
9bc2393c-3ee9-5329-9801-b1c119d8e1b3.description:
The luxurious Benz 8/20HP Grand Landaulet is every bit as grand as the name suggests. A favourite amongst high society, the Grand Landaulet was mainly a chauffeur-driven affair. The driver or chauffeur operated the vehicle from the more exposed section at the front, while the owners benefited from the added comfort of a luxurious cabin.  
  
Optional extras for this Benz were limited to acetylene lanterns and a horn. But the model itself enjoyed a relatively peaceful existence until its obsolescence.  
  
Its main extravagance was in the sheer choice of carriages available to the owners, who could opt for several open and closed body types.  
  
The Portuguese owner of this chassis, Dr. António de Matos Cid, opted for the most refined carriage of them all: the bulky and expensive Landau.  
  
The Landaulet body fitted to this car weighs in at a whopping 200 kg more than, for example, the De-Course, a more open and less ostentatious carriage.

9c9213a8-28c2-5a2e-b2db-b4b6a1e7014f.name: Cappadocian hand-made doll
9c9213a8-28c2-5a2e-b2db-b4b6a1e7014f.short_description: This doll represents a mother holding her baby over her head and It is one of the most precious objects of the museum. The production of this kind of rag doll was started by the women in the village called Soğanlı in Kayseri, a province in the central Anatolian region.  This tradition was then diffused throughout Cappadocia, and as the practice became more widespread it lead to the production of rags dolls with local patterns and motifs particular to that area. The rag dolls were simply made using wooden sticks, cloth and rag. Each of them has a unique size and unique clothes which represent the culture of the region. The doll spinning wool and the doll carrying a clay pitcher are very popular compositions, representing daily life.

9d51960b-dfb8-57bd-aa72-d264926dc7d8.name: The Presentation of the Virgin Mary into the Temple
9d51960b-dfb8-57bd-aa72-d264926dc7d8.description: This icon shows the presentation, or entrance, of the Virgin Mary into the temple. The story derives from the apocryphal book of James and is one of the 12 major feasts of the liturgical year, celebrated on November 21. This icon shows the child Mary before the priest Zacharias, father of John the Baptist. Mary’s parents, Anna and Joachim, stand with a group of maidens who also serve in the temple. Mary is seen again in the sacristy being approached by an angel.

Its silk fabric combined with copper wire allowed the wearer to shape it with her hands to create an object in the form she desired.

a43858e3-8e59-51e3-a4ad-791bad0297de.name: AC generator
a43858e3-8e59-51e3-a4ad-791bad0297de.description: In 1891, Charles Brown of Great Britain and Walter Boveri of Germany started an electrical engineering business in canton of Aargau. During its first year, Brown, Boveri & Co. had 70 employees. Only ten years later, that number had grown to over 1500. This steep increase was partly due to the success of the alternating current generator which the company began to produce in 1895. Europe was just discovering the benefits of electricity and demand was growing by the day. Switzerland had been an immigration country for generations and offered its new residents opportunities to realise their entrepreneurial dreams. In addition to Brown and Boveri, these immigrant entrepreneurs included the Austrian Carl Franz Bally, the founder of the shoe factory that bears his name, as well as the German pharmacist Henri Nestlé. Other famous brands like Rolex, Maggi, and Hero also owe their existence to the initiative of immigrants. The Jacobs, Hayeks, and Huxleys of this world continue to drive the Swiss economy to this day – just like a powerful generator.

a60a41df-2645-5a9b-be74-1fb21d8a5c13.description:

a8ca38d3-efce-510e-9b50-a7b6eb0e9a12.name: Bugatti Type 57C Atalante
a8ca38d3-efce-510e-9b50-a7b6eb0e9a12.description:
The Bugatti Type 57, unveiled at the 1934 Paris motor show, was a completely new design strongly influenced by Jean Bugatti, son of the company’s founder, Ettore. In 1936, Bugatti launched the 57C, which was fitted with a low-pressure Roots compressor, adding another 20 horsepower to the extraordinary engine. Hydraulic brakes were also introduced in 1938, making the 57C probably the best road-going Bugatti at the time. The Atalante was specially designed for long-haul travel, and many wealthy families crisscrossed Europe in them at leisure between the two world wars – a very fashionable habit during that period.  
  
Production ended in 1939 because of World War II and never resumed, making the Type 57 the fifth and last Bugatti to leave Molsheim – the Alsace factory where Ettore Bugatti was “Le Patron”. Between 1936 and 1940, Bugatti produced 82 units of a model based on the Type 57. Its sole aim was to be the world’s fasted touring car –something Ettore Bugatti was very eager to boast. That model, named the Type 57 Galibier, sporting four doors and four seats, achieved the record speed of 195 km/h in the hands of Robert Benoist on 27 May 1939.  
  
The Type 57 Atalante in the Museu do Caramulo has a unique aluminum bodywork. It was designed by Casa Vanvooren at the request of buyer Chaussivert, who wished to have a three-seater elongated Atalante. Measuring 5.37 meters between bumpers, it is 37 cm longer than the standard model.

a8f026f4-31f9-56e7-8410-813ac422bcf1.name: Alfa Romeo Giulia *Carabinieri*
a8f026f4-31f9-56e7-8410-813ac422bcf1.description: Sporty model produced from 1962 to 1977 in a wide variety of body styles. The technical quality of the Giulia project was widely exploited by Alfa Romeo, so much so that almost all the models presented up until the release of the Alfetta and Alfasud were based in one way or another on the Giulia. For many years, this car was the exclusive equipment of the Polizia (Italian National Police), the Carabinieri, the Guardia di Finanza (Financial Brigade) and the Army, because of its performances and driving qualities.

a98831d9-536c-5277-9779-66a5c608c1a8.name: Serpent glass *à la façon de Venise*
a98831d9-536c-5277-9779-66a5c608c1a8.description: The delicate nature and dainty shape of Venetian glasses are still fascinating today. The fragile glass is supported by an ornate “serpent stem” with white spiral threads. The shape is characteristic of Venetian glass, which, in the form of valuable wine glasses, adorned opulent tables in the 17th century. North of the Alps, Venetian glass was a term for highest quality colourless fine glass mass. For a long time, these glasses, produced in Venice using a perfect technique to achieve an elegant shape, were seen as the yardstick for glass-making. Glass works north of the Alps tried to imitate these glasses. In the 16th century, glass-blowers who had fled from Venice started to establish their own works in other parts of Europe. Their products gave rise to the term *à la façon de Venise*. This term was used for glassware from the 16th and 17th century, mainly for glasses made from decolourised glass mass and for shapes that were less common north of the Alps. With the rise of Bohemian and English glassware in the 18th century, Venetian glass lost its exclusivity.

aa3d92ab-8ac6-563e-ac59-78aeb1947c64.name: Snow cannon
aa3d92ab-8ac6-563e-ac59-78aeb1947c64.description: «Switzerland’s peaks are virtually devoid of snow, but in Savognin the snow falls from clear skies» wrote the newspaper Bündner Tagblatt on 9 December 1978. On that day, ten snow cannons provided enough snow for a three-kilometre piste on a green slope in the canton of Graubünden. When the first major artificial snow-blowing system in Europe went into operation, this marked the dawn of a new era in winter tourism. The snow cannons that caused a stir at the time are taken for granted today in every skiing resort of any size. Snow cannons were invented in Canada in 1940, when a team of researchers was studying the icing up of jet engines in a wind tunnel. While spraying water into a running turbine at sub-zero temperatures, the scientists had to contend with an undesirable side-effect: snow, which kept accumulating at the rear of the wind tunnel. What was an annoyance to those early researchers later became one of the biggest innovations in sports.

aa5417bd-aa61-5f36-9773-6c9fbf9885ab.name: Customised Toyota Truck
aa5417bd-aa61-5f36-9773-6c9fbf9885ab.description:
Almost unrecognisable, this Toyota Land Cruiser, once produced in Japan, is transformed into a decorated Pakistani truck. Fitted with a barrel, it was used for the transportation and distribution of water. The truck exhibits a large tank with a painted mural: decorative vegetal motifs of branches, leaves, and trees, along with lobed arches, ornamental oval medallions, intersecting geometric designs, architectural depictions and bird motifs such as the peacock.  
  
Mughal traditions of embellishing carts and carriages survived as an expression of art, national identity and personal taste. Motifs, such as the peacock, religious sites like the Kaaba, and flowers and vegetation narrate the storied heritage of Pakistani truck art and their owners.

aa631f7f-3808-586d-b316-c8c2c17e2045.name: The Royal Doors
aa631f7f-3808-586d-b316-c8c2c17e2045.description:
In Russian Orthodox churches, the sanctuary, which contains the altar, is separated from the nave by a wall or screen called an iconostasis. A typical iconostasis has three doors. The “angel doors” are located on the right and left sides and sometimes depict the Archangels Michael and Gabriel. The “royal doors” are located in the center of the iconostasis and can only be entered at certain points during liturgical services by ordained clergy members. The use of the royal doors varies by local tradition, but they are typically opened during the reading of the Gospel and distribution of the Eucharist. The royal doors typically depict the Annunciation while the four evangelists are shown on four separate panels.  
This set includes the symbol for each evangelist: Saint John is shown with a lion, Saint Luke with an ox, Saint Matthew with a man and Saint Mark with an eagle, following the famous interpretation of Saint Irenaeus (c.120-202). The symbol for Saint Mark is different than the one depicted in The Mother of God of the Burning Bush icon in this collection, reflecting a difference in the interpretation of biblical texts by the iconographers for each image.

aac7ff4c-14c4-5608-abb0-fe70488c219b.name: Breguet travel clock
aac7ff4c-14c4-5608-abb0-fe70488c219b.description: Organisers of major sporting events, mountaineers, and even astronauts rely on Swiss timepieces today. In the past, military strategists who made history swore by Swiss clocks. For example, Napoleon Bonaparte used a pocket watch by Abraham-Louis Breguet at the Battle of Waterloo in 1815. The clients of the watchmaker from the canton of Neuchâtel included not only the French general, but also his opponents: Both the Duke of Wellington and Field Marshal Gebhard Leberecht von Blücher devised their battle strategies with Breguet watches in their pockets. Apparently Breguet was more concerned with sales than with Swiss neutrality! Incidentally, Napoleon was a real Breguet fan and owned a total of three Breguet timepieces. The only one that has survived, however, is a travel clock kept in the Swiss National Museum.
keywords: Napoleon Bonaparte; Abraham-Louis Breguet; Clock; Paris

ad9d1414-7401-5672-ab97-813e0d702bd0.name: Porsche 911 2.0
ad9d1414-7401-5672-ab97-813e0d702bd0.description:
The successor to the Porsche 356, the 911 took the fundamental attributes of the popular sports car and multiplied its benefits. Bigger, wider, more rigid and above all, more powerful from its new and improved boxer engine, the 911 name quickly became synonymous with performance among Porsche fans. A prototype of the 911 broke cover for the first time at the 1963 Frankfurt Motor Show, and it instantly captivated the public. Baptised the 901, it was renamed 911 at the 1964 commercial launch due to a dispute over the naming rights with Peugeot. The coupé used a new two-litre six-cylinder boxer engine with 130hp – enough for a top speed of 210km/h.  
  
As with the 356, the new Porsche 911 was characterized by its build quality and the superb materials used in the cabin. What stood out more on the 911, though, was the technology under its skin. By installing the boxer engine behind the rear axle, the German engineers could not only develop a monocoque-type body, but also the suspension and braking system, creating a coupeé with a true sporting appeal.  
  
The constant evolution policy traditionally employed by Porsche led to the launch of the 911 S version in 1966 – the first to be equipped with the famous Fuchs alloy wheels. At the end of that year, they introduced the novel Targa body – their first attempt to transform the 911 into a convertible. The new Targa was fitted with a permanent roll bar to further improve passenger safety. In 1969 the Porsche 911 saw the displacement of its boxer engine rise to 2.2 litres. The transmission was also changed to Porsche’s Sportomatic semi-automatic box with four ratios in 1967.  
  
According to factory records, this Porsche was completed in October 1966, finished in Irish green lacquer, and trimmed with optional tinted windows, shield plugs, a left rear-view mirror, chrome rims and a Blaupunkt Frankfurt radio. The engine in this model is the 130hp two-litre six-cylinder type 901/05 boxer unit, which delivers that power at 6,100 revolutions per minute. Theis coupeé, with registration number LB-78-87, is equipped with the original five-speed manual type 902/1 gearbox.  
  
In September 2012 theis vehicle was recognized by Porsche Ibérica who issued it with a Certificate of Authenticity.

b0b3ea95-bfe9-538d-8ad1-b3b493bbb3aa.name: Ford Capri Group 2
b0b3ea95-bfe9-538d-8ad1-b3b493bbb3aa.description: This car was prepared by Ford Motorsport Köln in accordance with FIA Group 2 regulations. The Ford Capri Group 2 accumulated an impressive racing record in the 1971 and 1972 seasons in the hands of Gérard Larousse, Jochen Mass, Dieter Glemser and Carlos Soler-Roig with victories at Salzburgring 1971, Paul Ricard 24H 1971, Madrid 4H Jarama 1971 and 1972 and in Barcelona (Montjuich) 1972. But the most impressive result was the victory of Glemser/Soler-Roig in the 24H of Spa-Francorchamps in 1971, beating the Mercedes AMG 300 SEL 6.9 "Rote Sau".
b0b3ea95-bfe9-538d-8ad1-b3b493bbb3aa.author: Ahmed Chaouch

b0d054d9-1b44-564b-83f1-aa39fb7ee28d.name: Peugeot 402 Roadster
b0d054d9-1b44-564b-83f1-aa39fb7ee28d.description:
This 1937 black and silver convertible represents one of the rarest Peugeot 402 Roadster ever manufactured. By merging luxury and functional innovation, this vehicle would host a driver and a single passenger despite its enlarged size. This model also features safety door handles, an automatic transmission, and a clock incorporated within the dashboard.  
  
Despite the generous marketing in magazines, the second world war would affect the Peugeot 402’s demand. Focusing on combat and postwar reconstruction, the French longed for smaller models which would ultimately delay the next models by thirteen years.  
  
With its streamlined art deco design, this car still embodies the 1930s, a decade where car manufacturers like Citroen, Chrysler, and Bugatti, would compete for style and creativity.

b189b626-f957-5567-bfa3-5e00bd77ab99.name: Pontiac Star Chief
b189b626-f957-5567-bfa3-5e00bd77ab99.description:
This two-door red convertible with two “silver streaks” is a characteristic a classic car, cruising on forever in the memory of Qatar’s early days. Starting in 1954, the Star Chief would become the brand’s prestige limousine with luxury trims and chrome fender mouldings.  
  
In the US, the Pontiac division of General Motors witnessed a huge transformation in the 1950s. A beacon of luxury and performance, this second-generation convertible of the Star Chief series achieves 180 horsepower with Pontiac’s first V8 engine.  
  
The father of Sheikh Faisal Bin Qassim Al Thani once owned a car of this model and would drive his children to school in the old Msheireb district in the heart of Qatar’s capital.

b269b5d1-fa64-52f1-83ee-615537fde662.name: Golden bowl of Altstetten
b269b5d1-fa64-52f1-83ee-615537fde662.description: In Zurich, gold is something one expects to find in and around the financial centre at Paradeplatz. So you can imagine the surprise of the man working on the rail tracks in Altstetten in 1906 when his eye caught sight of a glint of gold shimmering through the mud. What came to light was a richly decorated bowl. It turned out to be one the most significant Bronze Age finds. The precious bowl had been lying in the ground, well protected, for about 3,000 years. Suns, full moons and crescents decorate the bowl. The noble material’s bright gloss also represents the heavenly lights. Even back in the Bronze Age people made use of the celestial bodies to orient themselves and keep track of the course of the seasons. They were aware of the sun and moon’s influence on the growth of crops and relied on them as symbols in their rituals.
keywords: archaeology; golden bowl; Altstetten

b2a09dfe-7666-5d5d-a174-97583427e649.name: Amphicar 770
b2a09dfe-7666-5d5d-a174-97583427e649.description: The most famous amphibian vehicle for private use. Two propellers provide propulsion on the water, with the front wheels acting as a rudder. As such the car is not particularly responsive on the water while its road handling is similarly awkward. The rear-fitted engine is that of a Triumph Herald, with a Porsche-developed gearbox. Between 1961 and 1968, 3,878 models were produced.
b2a09dfe-7666-5d5d-a174-97583427e649.author: Ahmed Chaouch

b72b1d9c-a54e-5011-9c5b-63ebd9004f3a.name: Portrait of two ‘spahis’ from the French Army interned in Estavayer-le-Lac (FR)
b72b1d9c-a54e-5011-9c5b-63ebd9004f3a.description: This portrait from late 1940 / early 1941 shows two “spahi”, probably from the Seventh Algerian Spahi Regiment, interned in Estavayer-le-Lac. This “spahi” regiment was part of the second mounted brigade of the 45th French army corps that fought a hard rearguard action as German tank units drove French forces into the Jura Mountains in June 1940. At the request of General Marius Daille, the French forces were granted asylum in Switzerland. During WWII, Swiss press photographers of necessity turned their attention to events at home. In the context of the “national spiritual defence” policy, many features were produced in which Switzerland was shown turned in upon itself, getting on with everyday life at a remove from the war going on around it. Interned soldiers represented one of the few real points of contact the Swiss had with the war. The North African cavalry in their unusual uniforms were a real attraction and proved a popular subject for a grateful Swiss press corps, and the photographer from the Presse Diffusion Lausanne (PDL) agency. The Swiss National Museum acquired the archives of Actualités Suisses Lausanne (ASL) and Presse Diffusion Lausanne (PDL) in 2007. Combined they number around six million images in the form of negatives, prints, and slides. Covering the years from 1937 to 1999, they record the most significant developments during the era of analogue press photography.

ba4e362f-15ff-5fee-b20f-edc0e07d2d14.name: Tunic (uniform). Officer of the "Cent-Suisse" (Swiss Hundred Guard)
ba4e362f-15ff-5fee-b20f-edc0e07d2d14.description: Officer of the "Cent-Suisse" in gala uniform, carrying a pole weapon called a spontoon. The oldest Swiss Hundred Guard comprising 109 men and 4 officers was established in 1497 as a bodyguard for the French king and performed sentry duties within French royal palaces, while the Swiss Guards Regiment undertook outside duties. The "Cent-Suisse" soldiers functioned purely as guards for the royal households, and were dressed and equipped accordingly. Based on their example, the papal company of Swiss Guards was established in 1506, and it exists to this day. Other monarchs, including those of the Netherlands, Savoy, Austria, Brandenburg-Prussia, and the Electorate of Saxony, later also recruited Swiss Guards. The Swiss Hundred Guard was disbanded in 1792 during the French Revolution.

be757c21-485f-5bb4-a983-8d72db9d4a64.name: Cisitalia 202 SMM Nuvolari
be757c21-485f-5bb4-a983-8d72db9d4a64.description: The model on display is the second of two cars that arrived at the Museum from the exchange with Brian Brunkhorst in 1995. Brunkhorst bought it in 1988 from a Ferrari dealer, and it came from South America. It had belonged to the same owner from 1948 to 1980, The previous owner, notary Federico Andreini from Buenos Aires, kept this car from 1948 to 1980 and raced with several times in Argentina. Andreini was a member of the Argentine CAS (Club de Automóviles Sport), a club set up just after the Second World War and dedicated to racing sports cars in Argentina. The four-cylinder in-line engine, derived from the Fiat 1100, displaces 1,089 cubic centimetres to provide 60–65 horsepower at 5,500 revolutions per minute; with it, this model can attain speeds of up to 180km/h.

bf743b8c-3b55-5eca-9558-3f933909bf96.name: Document chest
bf743b8c-3b55-5eca-9558-3f933909bf96.description: Chests are some of the oldest types of furniture and, depending on their size and construction, were used for storing or transporting documents, linen or food. The chest with its four locks from the St. Urban monastery in Canton Lucerne was used to store important documents and valuable books. The distinctive iron fittings served as protection and decoration. Chests were used in rural areas until the 19th century. Over time they were replaced by more convenient cupboards and chests of drawers.

c4ba74ec-5d96-5dd1-9cc3-a2a1553b4630.name: The Solovetsky Monastery
c4ba74ec-5d96-5dd1-9cc3-a2a1553b4630.description: Savvaty, a monk from the Kirilov Monastery, founded a small commune on the island of Solovki near the White Sea in 1392. He left the inhospitable island in 1435 and died later the same year. The next year, the monk Zosimas moved to Solovki and built the first monastic cell, which eventually became a splendid and wealthy monastery thanks to a lucrative salt trade and plentiful gifts. Zosimas remained the abbot until his death in 1478.  The monastery, with its numerous towers and thick, fortified walls, is depicted in the lower half of this icon, and Saints Zosimas and Savvaty are depicted above the monastery, flanked by two angels. This icon’s large scale and thematic content suggest that the image was produced at the Solovetsky Monastery.

c57df15d-93f3-5f9e-bece-295781bfd341.name: British incendiary bomb from World War II
c57df15d-93f3-5f9e-bece-295781bfd341.description: Composed of a steel shell and a detonator, this bomb weighs around 6.2 kg and is 82.5 cm long. It is connected to a cotton parachute measuring 35cm in diameter. When the parachute opened, the bomb was armed; it was intended also to allow the bomb to strike the ground upright, point first – only in this way was it able to detonate. By the time of the armistice on 22 June 1940, Nazi Germany had occupied northern France and had effective control of the south of the country. Eight days later, a British bomber jettisoned this incendiary device at 0100 hours on 30 June 1940 above Altmatt in central Switzerland. Although the warring parties were prohibited from flying over neutral Switzerland, its airspace was regularly violated. It is not known why the bomb was jettisoned, but it certainly failed to detonate on impact. The Swiss Army impounded the unexploded bomb, and on 4th July 1940, the signals battalion produced a report that is restricted to a detailed technical description of its construction and workings. Made in Norwich and dropped over Switzerland one summer’s night, this World War II bomb was finally handed over to the Swiss National Museum in 1976.

c6264581-3528-583b-bf88-dd6f925c33b8.name: Volkswagen *Carocha* Type 11 Export
c6264581-3528-583b-bf88-dd6f925c33b8.description:
Conceived as a means of transport for the masses, the Volkswagen “Beetle” emerged from the ashes of World War II to face the plethora of "micro-cars" on the world market. Offering a very competent and frugal engine, a platform-type chassis with a central tube and a build quality unrivalled in the segment, the Beetle quickly gained plenty of supporters. This in turn led Volkswagen to implement an annual improvement process that adapted the car to the needs of each country.  
  
Proposed by Adolf Hitler in the 1930s as the means of transport for Nazi Germany, the design of the Volkswagen ("people’s car") was assigned to Ferdinand Porsche. The instructions to Porsche were quite strict. The car should be very basic but capable of carrying two adults and three children. It should also maintain a speed of 100 km/h whilst using seven litres or less of fuel per 100 km. Parts were also to be inexpensive and easily replaceable and the engine should be air-cooled. Sold new in the Netherlands, the 1952 grey “Beetle” Type 11 Export in Museu do Caramulo maintains its original details down to the very last. This includes the red paint on the rims and bumpers which were specific to the Dutch market. Typical for the period, the rear window is split and the B-pillars are fitted with manual indicators. Being an export version, this Beetle has a higher level of trim detail compared to the standard model.

c73dca1b-c179-593d-9ff2-c9e643811ee8.name: Abu Radan Dress
c73dca1b-c179-593d-9ff2-c9e643811ee8.description: Black dress with wide, open sleeves, made from cotton fabric with heavy embroidery. The chest panel shows geometrical motifs (fans) on a rose-coloured collar. The shoulders show an embroidered emblem that is known as *nishan*, and the sleeves are heavily embroidered with cypress trees and waves that include yellow braid work along the length of the sleeve. The side panels of the dress (*banayeq*) show braid work with floral motifs topped by a scissor motif (*maqas*). The lower front panel of the dress shows motifs of cypress branches in different colours. The back shows the Pasha’s tent motif bordered by geometrical figures and cypress branches, while the bottom edge of the back panel has two blue lines that go around the dress. This type of dress was used mainly for celebrations and was worn by unmarried women only for events like weddings and women-only parties. These dresses were produced by hand by the same women who wore them, thus demonstrating the female’s ability to be productive. The origins of this dress lie in Bir al-Sabe, which is one of the largest cities in Palestine and is also known as the capital of the Negev desert. Some Bir al-Sabe inhabitants are originally Bedouin tribes, which explains why the women of Bir al-Sabe used to wear these heavy dresses. The garment has the advantage of being heavy, which helps the wearer cope with the desert climate in that region; it prevents sand from entering the women’s bodies and protects them from the heat. The dress is only worn by the women of Bir al-Sabe, and it is unique to them in respect of all the colours, stitches and motifs that the dress exhibits. It is worth mentioning that while Palestinian traditional costumes are distinguished by their individuality and regionalism, they still exhibit the influence of the different stages of occupation that Palestine has witnessed throughout its long history. In this case, the Ottoman influence is reflected in the long sleeves of the dress.

c8a7c58e-d37a-5d59-9506-320c260a750e.name: Saint Nicholas of Zaraisk with Various Scenes
c8a7c58e-d37a-5d59-9506-320c260a750e.description: Saint Nicholas, a 4th-century bishop from modern-day Turkey, is one of the most venerated saints in Russia. He is known as a protector of the weak and poor. Stories of Saint Nicholas giving gifts to the needy and protecting children spread far and wide as people traveled or emigrated from Russia to other countries. In this icon, Saint Nicholas is shown full-length, giving a blessing with his right hand while holding the Bible with his left. He is flanked by images of the Mother of God and Christ. The images in the border depict important moments from his life.

c96bfc16-fc32-5c92-ba26-346b59787f48.name: GMC Sierra
c96bfc16-fc32-5c92-ba26-346b59787f48.description:
This bus celebrates the South Asian truck art (phool patti in Urdu). This art form dates back to the Mughal dynasty (16th-19th century), where artists would break the boredom of long journeys by customising their vehicles with elaborate paintings, mirrors, and wood trimmings.  
  
Pakistani traditions inspire infinite constellations of peacocks, jasmine flowers, and talismanic eye motifs. The jingle truck’s name echoes the clinking sound of bells and pendants dangling above the pavement.  
  
The truck art helped ease the homesickness felt by lorry and bus drivers, incorporating messages of identity, belonging, and faith through calligraphy and idols. Pakistani patterns harmonise chaotic images like a kaleidoscope, brightening up life on the road and even influencing today’s fashion, including designs by Dolce&Gabanna and truck-artist Haidar Ali.

cb646540-71b4-53fd-9b5d-065a402f6c3b.name: 'Hortus Conclusus' church tapestry
cb646540-71b4-53fd-9b5d-065a402f6c3b.description: In our time, people who want to improve their logic skills might do a Sudoku while commuting on the urban railway. In medieval times, people would spend their time decoding the immense iconographic programme of the Catholic Church, which included not only Biblical figures and saints, but also legendary creatures with no religious connotations. The creator of the “Enclosed Garden” that can be seen on a precious tapestry from the chapel of Ried in what is today the canton of Schwyz drew on the early Christian natural history treatise known as the Physiologus, which states that a unicorn can only be captured by a virgin. From a Christian viewpoint, the virgin is Mary and her touching the unicorn’s horn is an allusion to the immaculate conception. Interpreting this scene correctly was tricky, but within the capabilities of medieval churchgoers. In contrast, they were less adept at understanding written letters and numbers.

cbc186ab-178b-5cb0-ad00-01955ebb8916.name: Reynard 903
cbc186ab-178b-5cb0-ad00-01955ebb8916.description:
It was 1990, when, after the famously close duel with Mika Häkkinen, Michael Schumacher won the Formula 3 Macau Grand Prix at the wheel of this Reynard 903.  
  
After winning Formula 3000 in 1989 with the 893 model, Reynard set its sights on improving still further. Maintaining the general specification of the previous model, improvements on the 903 focused only on aerodynamics. The car however, was not easy to drive, nor was it often fast; as a result, a lot of the drivers who had to pay for their drives opted for the rival Ralt RT34.  
  
Häkkinen’s dramatic victory and subsequent abandonment on the final lap (after the collision with Michael Schumacher) ensured the Reynard 903 would be a legend in the history of world motorsport forever.

cc245129-4801-5914-b91d-808b41eb1656.name: Al-Jilaya / Mardan Dress
cc245129-4801-5914-b91d-808b41eb1656.description: *Al-Jilaya* dress with large, open sleeves and heavy embroidery. The chest panel shows *qalayed* (necklace) embroidery and floral and geometrical motifs. The neck and shoulders are made with Ottoman striped fabric and the sleeves show patches of silk *hirmizi* fabric. The front panel of the dress has triangular shapes of silk with embroidered flowers. The *banayeq* (side panels) show rings and *Al-reesh* braid work, along with geometrical and floral motifs. The back panel has heavy and relatively long embroidery work, taking the shape of waves and geometrical figures, and is bordered with *Al-nakhl* and *Al-reesh* braid work. This is a handmade dress produced by the women of Hebron District and it is worn by married women for special occasions, especially weddings.

cd32766f-258a-52aa-a9db-291106450f76.name: Citroen 2CV
cd32766f-258a-52aa-a9db-291106450f76.description:
The Citroen 2CV attracts car-enthusiasts with its iconic appearance. Being a real car of the masses at an affordable price made the 2CV into the obvious choice for Europeans. In fact, demand was so high that it resulted in over 50 years of production for this Citroen.  
  
While allowing sufficient space for children and luggage, the lightweight wagon would stay steady on the fast highways and ice covered country roads.  
  
The well-known indigo colour remains one of the most sought-after paint hues for this series. Not to be missed in any car collection, the romanticised utilitarian vehicle impresses with its robust design and unique concept of a "world car".

cd8363f9-fa9a-5f8b-942e-3c9d931124ec.name: Saint Paraskeva
cd8363f9-fa9a-5f8b-942e-3c9d931124ec.description:
Saint Paraskeva was born to Christian parents during the reign of Emperor Hadrian. She was given the name Paraskeva (Greek for “Friday”) since Friday was the day of Christ’s crucifixion as well as the day of her birth. She was arrested during the reign of Emperor Antoninus Pius for preaching Christianity. He offered her great wealth and even proposed marriage if she renounced her faith, but she refused. The enraged emperor placed her in boiling oil, and when she did not show any pain, demanded to know whether she had used magic to cool the oil. She responded by throwing the hot liquid at the emperor, instantly blinding him. He asked Paraskeva for help and she healed him with water from a nearby stream. Antoninus Pius set her free, converted to Christianity and stopped persecuting Christians. The inscription on the scroll in this icon reads as follows:  
  
\[H\]ighly praised is thy name – of Father and Son and Holy Spirit, my Lord God – now and forever. For thou forgave me and did not reject my humility nor my prayer; and thy being pleased by me is incomprehensible.

cdec0b9e-508c-5b60-8df7-7a003023f3fe.name: Swiss Confederation 20 Franc coin
cdec0b9e-508c-5b60-8df7-7a003023f3fe.description: This Swiss 20 Franc gold coin minted between 1897 and 1949 is commonly known by its nickname «Gold Vreneli», from the diminutive form of the traditional Swiss girl’s name of Verena and the portrait of a lady on its obverse, as designed by Fritz Ulisse Landry (1842–1927). In April 1895 the Swiss Federal Council appointed a jury to assess the 21 design entries for a new gold coin. Among those who submitted designs were such famous names as the artist Albert Anker and the academic Friedrich Imhoof-Blumer. Fritz Ulisse Landry’s design won second prize; no first prize was awarded. The first 400,000 of these new gold coins were minted in 1897. In addition, 29 gold coins were produced using gold extracted from the mine at Gondo (Valais) that was abandoned that same year. This is one of the few remaining «Gondo-Vrenelis».

d2e14578-6d14-5f7d-85be-43b1df94ecf2.description: The Madonna, originally from Zurich and reminiscent of antique statues in posture and clothing, was imported from Northern Italy. d7822972-f602-5f72-804b-41aadb287492.name: Amber/Mardan Dress
d7822972-f602-5f72-804b-41aadb287492.description: Dress made of taffeta fabric (*Al-Alam*) with chest panel in *Al-Amber* style, which is a square with geometrical shapes and floral motifs on it. The top corner of the front panel has russet velveteen trim which extends along the shoulders. The dress also has large, long sleeves with geometrical motifs embroidered on the forearm and sleeve edges. The *banayeq* (side panels) show floral motifs while the back panel shows four thick braids in the style of *Al-Qasab* needlework. The women of Beit Jala (in the Bethlehem area) embroider and sew this garment on their own, and married women wear it on a daily basis. The Bethlehem area is considered to be the centre of culture and tourism in Palestine and also has religious significance as the birthplace of Jesus. Bethlehem is famous for its traditional and religious artifacts and colourful embroidery. This dress is very distinct because it is very practical and comfortable, it guarantees ease of movement and work, and it exhibits outstanding colour.

d97e8889-9ee3-5eb8-9ea9-a6732fa73dbd.description: This Mother of God icon is known as a *Hodegetria* icon (Greek for “one who shows the way”). It is recognizable by the solemn expression of the Mother of God and the frontal position of the Christ Child delivering a blessing. The Christ Child sits on his mother’s left knee and holds a tightly rolled scroll. A copy of the original *Hodegetria* icon was brought to the Assumption Cathedral in Smolensk from Byzantium in the 12th century. In the 15th century, it was transferred to Moscow before being returned to Smolensk. The icon has a silver *repoussé basma* (hammered metal ornamentation) nailed to its surface, as well as a Kremlin School *cloisonné* raised halo dating back to the 17th century.

d9bac10e-6db4-531b-92e6-aec10ee3135d.name: Lamborghini LM002
d9bac10e-6db4-531b-92e6-aec10ee3135d.description:
This white-on-red SUV marks a surprising endeavour for Lamborghini – a brand known for sports cars. Challenging all expectations, the LM002 represents the third among Lamborghini’s off-road vehicles, following the Cheetah and the LM001.  
  
With only 328 models produced worldwide, the rare civilian model offers all customary luxuries outfitted in the military truck. The massive exterior of the so-called Rambo-Lambo camouflages numerous curiosities within the snug interior including a battery power switch, storage in rear seats and a stereo mounted on the ceiling.  
  
Whilst Lamborghini commissioned special Pirelli Scorpion tyres to soar through the desert, its most daring feature remains the impressive V12-engine, borrowed from the Lamborghini Countach. The desert-yacht ranges between 455-600 horsepower and prevails as an all-time favourite of bizarre car creations.

dd807bf3-fa34-5d58-a1c7-ca19e5e0b06b.name: Ford T
dd807bf3-fa34-5d58-a1c7-ca19e5e0b06b.description:
As the first car to be affordably mass-produced, the Ford Model T is one of the most important cars in automobile history. Although there were some Model T’s manufactured before 1909, assembly-line production began properly in 1909. This specimen is one of the first produced in this way.  
  
Our Model T was imported to Portugal in 1909, but it was only on 27 November, 1911, that it saw proper use. This was because the then-recent Law of Brito Camacho caused a disruption in car traffic in the north and south of Portugal.  
  
Its first registered owner was António Augusto Correia, who registered it with the plate N-373. In 1927, the car was to change hands when Manuel Menéres, after seeing it at the Mirandela fair, exchanged it with his modern 1926 Ford.  
  
Menéres used it in several events, including the Estoril Rallye of Vintage Cars in 1932, the Rallye de Santo Tirso, in 1962, and the International Rallye of Estoril, in 1964.  
  
On 29 May, 1968, this Model T was certified by the Veteran Car Club of Great Britain and given the number 1,146.  
  
With engine number 11340, it is in fact amongst the first batch of cars to roll off Ford’s assembly line in 1909. The total number of Model T’s manufactured that year exceeded 15,000 units—a testament to Henry Ford’s mass production vision.

The Museum of Russian Icons has ten icons from the original set.

df551296-3682-582b-a97b-05ba149fa548.name: Constant Delessert, double exposure
df551296-3682-582b-a97b-05ba149fa548.description: Adrien Constant de Rebecque, better known as Constant Delessert, was a typical child of the nineteenth century, an age of great change. In his role as a pioneer of photography he experimented with various techniques, such as double exposure. This allowed Delessert to arrange portraits and self-portraits in such as a manner that it looked like two individuals were interacting, although, in fact, it was the same person exposed twice in short sequence but in different roles. In the present picture Delessert is looking at himself while reading. The play with cultural stereotypes – his double exposures include pictures of servants, portrait painters as well as beggars – in combination with the, often delayed, realization that one is dealing with one and the same person, makes this series so remarkable. Together with other museums, the Swiss National Museum was able to purchase ten albums with works by Constant Delessert at an auction, five of which are now in the National Museum collection. They contain portraits, natural scenes, architectural images as well as street views. They visualize the Switzerland of Delessert’s era in a remarkable way. Delessert, who came from an affluent family, also staged and documented with the help of images of poor people, servants and peasants how, in those days, clothing embodied visible social boundaries.

e042ddd9-4096-5b3f-86de-810559520343.name: Citroën 15 – Six D *Traction Avant*
e042ddd9-4096-5b3f-86de-810559520343.description:
In 1933, André Citroën started developing his dream car, the Traction Avant. It would have a mono-block engine, front-wheel drive and an automatic gearbox, the use of which would later be abandoned. Development of the new Citroën model was never short of problems, but the banks who had invested thousands of francs in Citroën put pressure on the company to go to market. The result was catastrophic, culminating in hundreds of warranty claims.  
  
Shortly after the bankruptcy of the brand bearing his name was declared, André Citroën, now penniless, died on the 5 July 1935. However, his dream car was to be produced, to significant success, after Michelin paid off Citroën’s debts and went ahead with the production of the Traction Avant.  
  
A few years after the launch of the Citroën 15-Six, João de Lacerda acquired one, which he used for road trips and automobile races like the XXI Rally de Monte Carlo, in 1951. One year later, accompanied by Jaime Azarujinha, he participated in the same rally – this time in a Citroën “Drag”. Departing from seven cities in Europe, the race coincided with very heavy snowfall—making it one of the toughest editions ever in the history of the event. Of the 328 cars present at the start, only 163 would cross the finish line. And out of those, only 15 were without any penalties, with João de Lacerda counted amongst them. Lacerda would repeat the grueling test on two more occasions in 1953 and 1954 in the same Citroën to claim the ACP Trophy.  
  
After several years of intense service, divided between daily use and participation in several national and international competitions, the two Citroën 15-Sixes belonging to João de Lacerda were scrapped. This gave rise to the purchase of a similar model in France, which was restored in Portugal with the help of Jacques Touzet and Antero Marques Paiva.  
  
As a prize for the magnificent restoration, the famous license plate, HF-16-83, used with great success in the 1952, 1953 and 1954 editions of the Monte Carlo Rally, was recovered by the official entities and presented to the “new” Citroën 15-Six, which today is in Museu do Caramulo.

e204df2a-1723-53bc-98dd-25fd21837af9.name: Bracelet
e204df2a-1723-53bc-98dd-25fd21837af9.description: Antoinette Riklin-Schelbert belonged to the avant-garde of Swiss jewellery makers. Trained as a silversmith, she ran her own studio and shop after 1946. She exhibited at national and international shows, published books, and gave lectures. She also held the post of president of the Swiss Crafts Council from 1986 to 1992. The SNM’s two collections – comprising Riklin-Schelbert’s own designs and those of other contemporary Swiss makers as well as her sketchbooks – reflect her role as a pioneer of experimental jewellery and her influence on other jewellery makers in Switzerland.

e27d0597-a9c7-5b41-b39b-1e74241036e3.name: FIAT 600 Multipla
e27d0597-a9c7-5b41-b39b-1e74241036e3.description:
In the years following World War II, it became apparent to Fiat that their future would be in small cars with low manufacturing costs, sold at affordable prices. Dante Giacosa, Fiat’s chief designer, was tasked with designing a replacement for the Topolino 500. Under the name of Project 100, and after several rounds of test and development—always with one eye on cost – a small vehicle with four seats took form. It was powered by a very simple but reliable rear-mounted four-cylinder engine. The car became known as the Fiat 600, one of the 20th century’s greatest automobile successes with about 2.7 million units produced.  
  
The Multipla launched at the 1956 Brussels motor show was an ingenious evolution of the brilliant little Fiat 600. Using the 600 as a base with an engine at the rear and the boot at the front, Fiat mounted the suspension from their wider 1100 models, creating ample space for luggage between the seats and the engine compartment. Thus, the 600-line was expanded for both family and commercial use.  
  
The newly launched multi-seat Fiat 600 Multipla was uniquely versatile. Clever folding seats were combined with a chassis that could be fitted with the option of four, five, or six seats and even a taxi version.  
  
It was the first minivan sold with more than five seats whilst maintaining reduced exterior dimensions.

e48e1a08-e547-5d16-8d50-c1e235658222.name: Lotus Europa Special
e48e1a08-e547-5d16-8d50-c1e235658222.description:
In 1963, Lotus’s director of engineering, Ron Hickman, was approached by Ford for a collaboration on the legendary GT40 project. But the contract for Ford’s contender at Le Mans was awarded to rivals Lola Cars, which led Hickman and Lotus founder Colin Chapman revived their sketches in a bid to create a successor for the Lotus Type 7. In 1966 the Lotus Type 46 (also known as the Europa S1) was born. Like the Elan, the Lotus Europa also used a “double-Y” steel chassis which also served as the main support for the car’s mechanical components. However, instead of mounting the engine at the front, the Lotus Europa had a mid-mounted engine, the first for a mass-produced car.  
  
Originating from Colin Chapman’s pioneering ideas, the Lotus Europa was designed with independent suspension on all four wheels. The system was very similar to the one used on the Grand Prix cars of the time. The body of the Europa also made use of advances in engineering materials at the time, being innovatively moulded as a single-piece fibreglass construction. For the engine, Lotus turned to the French manufacturer Renault, opting for their 1470cc four-cylinder unit from the Renault 16, which Chapman coupled to a four-speed gearbox. Delivering 82hp, the French engine was enough to propel the 686kg Europa to 180km/h.  
  
In 1971, the TwinCam version of the Lotus Europa, the most powerful variant, was presented to the public. With the 1558cc four-cylinder big-valve engine and double overhead camshafts, the new Europa Type 74 outputted 115hp, giving the 730kg car an excellent power-to-weight ratio. A Renault 4-ratio gearbox was chosen to accompany the new engine. Additionally, the body underwent design changes which gave greater visibility through the rear window.  
  
A few months after the Europa TwinCam was introduced, Mike Kimberley, the Chief Engineer responsible for the Europa TC project, gave the order for the new cars to be equipped with Dell’Orto or Weber carburetors, a combination much celebrated on the Lotus Elan Sprint. Baptised the Europa Special, the updated model, fitted with a Renault five-speed gearbox delivered 126hp. Weighing in at 740kg, the Special had a top speed of 198km/h and could accelerate from zero to 100km/h in just seven seconds.  
  
In honor of the Formula 1 World Championships won in 1972 and 1973 by Team Lotus, a small volume of the Special was created, named the Europa John Player Special. Launched in black livery with the famous gold leaf bands, the John Player Special has become synonymous with the Europa name. It is still one of the most sought-after cars today.  
  
This car was donated to the Museu do Caramulo by Francisco da Cruz Martins.

e7789911-13d5-5689-9f57-6f31db64cdef.name: Jillayeh Wedding Dress
e7789911-13d5-5689-9f57-6f31db64cdef.description: Black dress with heavy embroidery. The chest panel shows chevron pattern embroidery, which is also known as *qalayed* (necklace), as well as many floral motifs, while the back panel shows floral motifs embroidered on silk fabric with special stitches. The sleeves are heavily embroidered with vine leaves, while the *banayeq* (side panels) show motifs of flowers, feathers and *manajel* (thick braid work connecting the dress parts). This dress is mainly worn by the married women of Hebron for ceremonial events like weddings. Located in the West Bank, south of Jerusalem, and founded by the Canaanites in the early Bronze Age, Hebron has been famous since ancient times for handicrafts, including ceramics, pottery, glass, embroidery and leather. This gown is handmade from silk and cashmere using atlas stitch. The dress is worn only by married women of Hebron, and it is unique to them in respect of all the colours, stitches, floral motifs and vine leaf motifs that the dress exhibits. The bottom front panel has yellow, orange and red silk triangles with Kashmir cloth on the sides. The bottom of the back panel has a stitched-in piece of cloth with blue embroidered birds and flowers. The use of birds and flowers does not bear any hidden symbolism; rather, it reflects the continuous work of women on the land and hence their use of nature as a main source of inspiration for their embroidery, not only in Hebron but other regions of Palestine as well.

e8585e51-819e-5872-8973-ce808037781d.short_description: This wooden car was manufactured by Çevik Toy Company in 1957. eb0069e6-ef9d-5223-afab-ebd48196c101.name: Sab’aawi Dress
eb0069e6-ef9d-5223-afab-ebd48196c101.description: Black dress with wide, long sleeves and *aqras* (geometrical figures) embroidered on the chest panel. The shoulders and upper sleeves show geometrical figures with cypress tree braid work. The sleeve opening has a *tashreefa* motif with white and red colours. The front panel and the *banayeq* (side panels) have heavy cypress tree motif embroidery, while the back panel shows an atlas motif with moons and geometrical figures. The top shows cypress tree designs and the bottom edge of the dress shows two lines of blue embroidery. This handmade dress originally comes from the Bir al-Sabe district. It is an everyday dress, and all women can wear it day to night. It is casual and comfortable, allowing them to do their house chores easily, and is also very practical and easy to wear.

ecf83ab7-6b66-5394-a33d-af56b082562e.name: Cadillac Series 62 Convertible
ecf83ab7-6b66-5394-a33d-af56b082562e.description:
In 1954, the Belgian Royal Palace’s car fleet expanded significantly with the addition of this Cadillac Series 62 convertible, which became the official parade vehicle. Featuring specifications ahead of its time for 1955, it proudly bore the Belgian number plate “1” and was predominantly used by King Baudouin. This impressive limousine embarked on a historic mission in 1955: During King Baudouin’s first trip to Congo, where he was welcomed as “Bwana Kitoko,” the Cadillac covered part of the 10,000-km journey.  
  
In 1959, the Series 62 served as the bridal car for Prince Albert and Paola’s wedding. A year later, King Baudouin and Queen Fabiola also celebrated their marriage in this Cadillac. To withstand the harsh winter weather during the latter wedding, coachbuilder "Vesters & Neirinck" constructed a transparent plexiglass dome, ensuring the newlyweds could sit warmly in the spacious rear seat while remaining visible to the many well-wishers.  
  
The car underwent several modifications to fulfill its royal duties. Notably, the front bench was divided into two sections, allowing the passenger side to slide back, enabling the occupant to stand upright and greet the crowd. Additionally, a handle was mounted on the windscreen pillar to facilitate standing without mishaps.  
  
After being sold by the royal family, the Cadillac’s missions became less historic. At one point in Paris, it was even used for public sightseeing tours. Autoworld is delighted to have been able to reunite the royal Cadillac Series 62 with other cars from the former royal fleet.
ecf83ab7-6b66-5394-a33d-af56b082562e.author: Ahmed Chaouch
